entries.sought: Exact integer algorithms for the proleptic Gregorian calendar: a date to a day count, back, and the weekday

sources.title: chrono-Compatible Low-Level Date Algorithms (Howard Hinnant)
sources.said: days_from_civil: y -= m <= 2; era = (y >= 0 ? y : y-399) / 400; yoe = y - era*400; doy = (153*(m > 2 ? m-3 : m+9) + 2)/5 + d-1; doe = yoe*365 + yoe/4 - yoe/100 + doy; return era*146097 + doe - 719468. civil_from_days is its inverse; weekday_from_days counts from Thursday 1970-01-01.

sources.title: ECMA-262, Time Values and Time Range
sources.said: Time values count milliseconds from 1970-01-01 UTC on the proleptic Gregorian calendar, the calendar the tests read Date against.

entries.sought: How zic turns rules and zone lines into transitions, to compute them the same way
entries.value: outzone (rules taken in UT order, a wall-clock moment read with the save in effect; a line ends at its until read with the save then; the start type from the last rule before it or the first standard-time rule after) and writezone's optimize pass

sources.title: zic.c, tz release 2026f (the tz development repository IANA names at data.iana.org/time-zones/tz-link.html)
sources.said: outzone, lines 3375 to 3685: per zone line, save = 0; for each year, the untried rule with the earliest jtime = r_temp - (r_todisut ? 0 : stdoff) - (r_todisstd ? 0 : save); stop when ktime >= untiltime (until less stdoff and save by its kind); rules before starttime set startoff and the start abbreviation; at the end, starttime = until less save and stdoff. writezone, lines 2670 to 2711: a transition whose local time (at + previous type's offset) is not later than the previous transition's (at + the type before it) replaces it, or removes it when it returns to that type; a transition to the same offset, isdst and abbreviation is dropped. Both ranges are line for line those of 2026e (outzone 3415 to 3725, writezone 2691 to 2732); 2026f's other changes to zic.c drop the leap second table's expiry.

sources.title: tz NEWS
sources.said: 2026b: zic versions 2023d through 2026a can mishandle a last transition to a new time type in slim output; use zic -b fat. 2026a: zic no longer generates a no-op transition when simultaneous Rule and Zone changes cancel each other out (Asia/Tbilisi, 1997-03-30). 2026f: zic now ignores Expires lines, as leap second tables no longer expire.

entries.sought: A published method for sunrise and sunset by latitude, longitude and date, with its accuracy
entries.value: NOAA GML solar calculator: Meeus's equations; 0.833° below the horizon; accurate to within a minute between 72°N and 72°S, within ten minutes beyond

sources.title: NOAA GML, Solar Calculation Details
sources.said: The calculations are based on equations from Astronomical Algorithms, by Jean Meeus. The sunrise and sunset results are theoretically accurate to within a minute for locations between +/- 72° latitude, and within 10 minutes outside of those latitudes. For sunrise and sunset calculations, we assume 0.833° of atmospheric refraction. The calculator is no longer actively supported or maintained.

sources.title: NOAA GML solar calculator, main.js
sources.said: calcGeomMeanLongSun, calcGeomMeanAnomalySun, calcEccentricityEarthOrbit, calcSunEqOfCenter, calcSunApparentLong, calcMeanObliquityOfEcliptic, calcObliquityCorrection, calcSunDeclination, calcEquationOfTime, calcHourAngleSunrise (cos 90.833°), calcSunriseSetUTC: timeUTC = 720 - 4*(longitude + hourAngle) - eqTime, refined once at JD + timeUTC/1440.

sources.title: NOAA GML, NOAA_Solar_Calculations_day.xls
sources.said: The worked day as published: 2010-06-21 at latitude 40, longitude -105, time zone -6, every six minutes; columns Julian Day, Julian Century, Geom Mean Long Sun, Geom Mean Anom Sun, Eccent Earth Orbit, Sun Eq of Ctr, Sun App Long, Mean Obliq Ecliptic, Obliq Corr, Sun Declin, Eq of Time, HA Sunrise and onward (xls sha256 1def11406d4548aba852aa303d9c9ac35f0896f55eeaeb6cc9b7bef4a1b90a99; read to values with LibreOffice into research/sources/sun/noaa-solar-calculations-day-2010-06-21.csv). entries.sought: Why the ICU time zones in Node (tz 2026e in Node 22.23.4) differ from the 2026f release for some zones
entries.value: Cuba stays on -04 through 2027-11-07 (America/Havana); Brazil's 1965 and 1966 DST ends, before 1970 and so outside the window compared

sources.title: tz NEWS, release 2026f
sources.said: Release 2026f - 2026-10-27. Cuba will not fall back to -05 on 2026-11-01 and instead plans to maintain -04 through 2027-11-07. In 1965 Brazil ended DST on 03-31 at 24:00 not 00:00, and in 1966 it ended DST on 03-01 at 01:00 not 00:00.

entries.sought: What VED denotes beside VES, after Venezuela's 2021 redenomination
entries.value: VED/926 represents the redenominated bolívar (1,000,000 times the old VES); VES/928 stays the valid code for the same redenominated bolívar

sources.title: ISO 4217 Amendment Number 170 (1 October 2021)
sources.said: The Bolívar Soberano (VES) is redenominated by removing six zeros from the denominations. A new currency code VED/926 representing the new valuation (1,000,000 times old VES/928) is introduced on 1 October 2021 for any internal needs during the redenomination process, but is not replacing VES as the official currency code. The Central Bank of Venezuela will not adopt the new codes in the local system, VES/928 remains in use. The actual currency code VES/928 remains the valid code after 1 October 2021 to use in any future transactions to indicate the redenominated Bolívar Soberano.

Bird International Airport is listed at 17.130, -62.371, some 60 km west of the airport, so its country is taken from the Member, not the nearest town. Three stations carry the placeholder location -98.6, -986.6 with ID 99999999 (Rwanda's BUGARAMA_RIZ, Guyana's Lama and Wakapow) and are left out, having no place on Earth. sources.title: NCEI, WMO Climate Normals
sources.said: The Global Climatological Standard Normals are calculated for a uniform 30-year period and consist of annual and monthly averages and statistics; NCEI, as host of the World Data Center for Meteorology, provides their stewardship. Earlier sets: 1981-2010 (about 55 countries) and 1961-1990.

entries.sought: The same normals, for the countries and parameters 1991-2020 lacks, from each country's own 1961-1990 submission

sources.title: Contents and arrangement of the 1961-1990 global climate normals (NCEI)
sources.said: Computed by the Member countries and territories of the WMO in the 1990s and submitted to NOAA's NCEI (World Data Center for Meteorology): over 4000 stations by more than 135 countries and territories.

sources.title: 1961-1990 normals data file format (DATA_FMT.TXT)
sources.said: Records by region, NCDC country code, WMO number and national id; columns 18-25 the period; 27-28 the element (01 dry bulb, 02 maximum, 03 minimum temperature, 06 precipitation, 15 sunshine, 40 bright sunshine, 95 days with precipitation of at least a threshold), 29-30 the statistic (01 mean value, 15 mean monthly value, 44 mean number of hours), 31-36 the qualifier (for 95, the threshold in mm); twelve monthly values of 7 characters each from column 38. Missing: -9999.9, -99999, -9999; trace: 88888.8, 8888888; above zero but under the smallest unit: -9797.9, -97979.

sources.title: 1961-1990 normals, countries and territories and their codes (CTRYCOD1.TXT)
sources.said: NCDC's own two-letter codes, not ISO's: among them VN Venezuela, GA Georgia, GN Gabon, GW Guinea, IL Iceland, IS Israel, MA Mauritius, MC the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia, NA Netherlands Antilles and Aruba, U1 United States (Pacific Islands), YG Yugoslavia.

sources.title: 1961-1990 station metadata format (STN_META.TXT)
sources.said: Station metadata: the Member's latitude (19-23, degrees, minutes, hemisphere) and longitude (24-29), elevation (30-35, m); WMO Publication No. 9's latitude (36-40), longitude (41-46) and elevation (47-50); the Member's station name (57-90), Publication No. 9's (91-136).

entries.sought: For the countries and parameters no published normal gives (the WMO's sets, the 1981-2010 normals, the national services', the Deutscher Wetterdienst's and the World Weather Information Service's): the mean daily maximum and minimum temperature, precipitation and days of at least 1 mm, as averages computed from a station's daily observations by the WMO's rules

value.stations: The 25 GHCN-Daily stations of Botswana, the Falkland Islands, Kuwait, Lebanon, Eswatini, Niue, Vanuatu, Suriname, Pitcairn and South Georgia with ten years or more of precipitation or temperature in 1991-2020 (by NCEI's ghcnd-inventory.txt), each placed in the country its identifier names (FIPS 10-4, by ghcnd-countries.txt); stations of other countries near them (Cumberland in South Africa, Changalane in Mozambique, Princess Juliana in Sint Maarten, East End in the U.S. Virgin Islands) left out.
value.rules: WMO-No. 1203 (2017): a day counts where its quality flag is blank; a month's mean is none where 11 or more days are missing or 5 or more in a row (4.4.1 a), a month's sum none where any day is (4.4.1 c), a month's count of days of at least 1 mm a share of the days observed, none by the mean's rule (4.3.1 d, 4.4.1 d); a month's average is the mean of its valid values, a count's mean share times the month's days, February's 28.25 (4.3.2), where they are of at least 80% of the averaging period's years (4.4.2). The averaging period, an average as chapter 3 defines it (over any period), is each parameter's longest within 1991-2020 of ten years or more, from a year with a month of it to another, whose every month is averaged so; the latest of the longest.
value.filled: Suriname's days of at least 1 mm (Johan A. Pengel, 2009-2020) and Pitcairn's maximum and minimum temperature (Pitcairn Island, 1991-2003); the other stations' records are too broken for an average of every month by these rules, or give what their country has from a published normal.

station.name: Roc St. Pere (Andorra la Vella), the Servei Meteorològic Nacional's station 99130005
station.months: 360 workbooks, each month of 1991-2020, each pinned by its SHA-256 in the file

value.rules: As R-0073's (WMO-No. 1203, 2017): a month's mean none where 11 or more days are missing or 5 or more in a row (4.4.1 a), a month's sum (precipitation, sunshine) none where any day is (4.4.1 c), a count of days of at least 1 mm a share of the days observed (4.3.1 d), its average the mean share times the month's days, February's 28.25 (4.3.2); each month's average the mean of its valid values where they are of at least 80% of the period's years (4.4.2); the period each parameter's longest within 1991-2020 of ten years or more, from a year with a month of it to another, whose every month is averaged so, the latest of the longest. Rounded to a tenth (half up). Computed by tools/wmo/compile.ts as the stations compile. A day's maximum is the workbook's 'màx 06-06', its minimum 'mín 18-18', its precipitation 'Precipitació 06-06 (mm)', its sunshine 'Insolació 00-24 (h)' ('5h 38' read as 5 h 38 min).
value.sunshine: The sunshine recorder failed: it read 0 h on nearly every day from July 2016 to June 2017, and through August 2014, under full sun (August 2016: 0 h every day, 2,000-2,900 J/cm² of global irradiation). A day of 0 h whose irradiation ('Irradiació 00-24') is over 60% of the month's highest is taken as the recorder's gap, not a reading, as the research agent screened it; a month with a gap has no sum, so the sunshine's period is 1992-2013 (18 to 21 years a month). Unscreened, 1992-2017 would give 118.8 to 241.1 h, the faulty zeros pulling every month down.
value.caveat: The service's page marks data awaiting validation in red ('les dades en vermell estan pendents de validar'); the workbooks don't carry the colour, so validated and unvalidated days are read alike.
value.ruling: An average computed from the service's own records, which the lead's ruling of 2026-11-02 lets stand as a normal, labelled to the player as R-0073's are (the official averages measured near a place, from the years they cover: weather.model).

value.rules: Each month's value as the CLIMAT report gives it (a monthly mean, a monthly sum, a count of days), averaged by WMO-No. 1203 4.4.2 as R-0073's: the mean of its values where they are of at least 80% of the period's years; the period each parameter's longest within 1991-2020 of ten years or more, from a year with a month of it to another, whose every month is averaged so, the latest of the longest; rounded to a tenth (half up). Each parameter from the latest historical file (the recent files begin in 2024, after 2020).
value.notFound: Grytviken's days of at least 1 mm stop in February 1982 (88903_196801_198202.txt): none in 1991-2020, so they stay blocked (R-0084). GHCN-Daily's Mount Pleasant and Grytviken records were too broken for R-0073's rules; the CLIMAT monthly series aren't.
value.ruling: An average computed from the service's own records, which the lead's ruling of 2026-11-02 lets stand as a normal, labelled to the player as R-0073's are (the official averages measured near a place, from the years they cover: weather.model).

sources.title: WMO Guidelines on the Calculation of Climate Normals, 2017 edition (WMO-No. 1203, ISBN 978-92-63-11203-3), the WMO's PDF as a copy hosts it (29 pages, made 2017-11-30); the WMO e-Library's own page answers with a check this environment can't pass
sources.said: Chapter 3: an average is the mean of monthly values over any specified period. 4.3.1-4.3.2: a count is a share of the days observed, its normal the mean share times the month's days, February's 28.25. 4.4.1: a mean is not calculated where 11 or more days are missing or 5 or more consecutive; a sum only with complete data; a count by the mean's rule. 4.4.2: a normal or average only where there are valid monthly values in at least 80% of the years of the averaging period.

entries.sought: The months of the calendars holidays are kept in other than the Gregorian (the Umm al-Qura Islamic, the Hebrew, the Chinese, the Korean, the Persian and the Ethiopian), 2000 to 2100

sources.title: ICU 78.3 (International Components for Unicode), its calendars as Node.js 22.23.4 ships them (all but the Chinese): islamcal.cpp (Umm al-Qura, its month lengths the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia's), hebrwcal.cpp, dangical.cpp, persncal.cpp, ethpccal.cpp
sources.said: Intl.DateTimeFormat with the calendars islamic-umalqura, hebrew, chinese, dangi, persian and ethiopic gives each day's year, month and day; 2026's: 1 Shawwal 1447 = 20 March, 10 Dhu al-Hijjah 1447 = 27 May, 1 Tishri 5787 = 12 September, 15 Nisan 5786 = 2 April, Chinese and Korean New Year = 17 February, 1 Farvardin 1405 = 21 March, 1 Meskerem 2019 = 11 September.

sources.title: ICU-23069 Fix Hebrew calendar calculation (2025-03-19, first released in ICU 78)
sources.said: hebrwcal.cpp's startOfYear: the postponement for a common year whose molad falls on a Tuesday after 9h 204p becomes an else-if of the one before it, so a year takes one postponement, not two. Compiled on ICU 77.1 (SLATE's), the Hebrew year 5806 began its months from Kislev a day late and 5807 on 2046-10-02; on ICU 78.3, 1 Kislev 5806 is 2045-11-10 and 1 Tishri 5807 is 2046-10-01, as Calendrical Calculations' rules give (5806 a leap year of 384 days) and as Hebcal's converter gives (read the same day). No other month of the six calendars from 2000 to 2100 moved.

sources.title: Hong Kong Observatory, Gregorian-Lunar Calendar Conversion Tables, 1999 to 2100 (https://www.hko.gov.hk/en/gts/time/calendar/text/files/T{year}e.txt), the Chinese calendar's
sources.said: A row a day: '2027/2/6  1st Lunar Month  Saturday' (Chinese New Year 2027), '2030/2/3  1st Lunar Month  Sunday'; a month whose number repeats is the leap month ('2025/6/25  6th Lunar Month', '2025/7/25  6th Lunar Month'). ICU 77.1's Chinese calendar begins six months a day off these tables in 2000-2100 (2012-08-18, 2018-11-07, 2027-02-07, 2030-02-02, 2057-09-29, 2070-03-13), so the tables are kept, not ICU. The 2069 table leaves out 2069/12/30, between 16 (12/29) and 18 (12/31) of one month: kept as 17.

sources.said: Quels sont les jours fériés légaux ? Le 1er janvier, le lundi de Pâques, le 1er mai (Fête du travail), l’Ascension, le lundi de Pentecôte, le 21 juillet (Fête nationale), le 15 août (l’Assomption), le 1er novembre (la Toussaint), le 11 novembre (l’Armistice), le 25 décembre (Noël). Si ce jour coïncide avec un dimanche ou un jour habituel d’inactivité dans l’entreprise, ce « jour de remplacement » sera nécessairement fixé sur un jour habituel d’activité dans l’entreprise.

entries.sought: Ireland's public holidays, the days off its law or its government's list names, nationally and in each first-level region that keeps its own

sources.title: Workplace Relations Commission, Public Holidays
sources.said: In Ireland there are ten public holidays each year. From 2023, there is a public holiday on the first Monday in February, except where 1st February falls on a Friday in which case that Friday 1st February will be the public holiday. Public holidays are: New Year’s Day (1st January); First Monday in February; St. Patrick’s Day (17th March); Easter Monday; First Monday in May; First Monday in June; First Monday in August; Last Monday in October; Christmas Day (25th December); St. Stephen’s Day (26th December). Good Friday is not a public holiday and is a normal working day. In 2026 the dates of these public holidays are as follows: 01 January, 02 February, 17 March, 06 April, 04 May, 01 June, 03 August, 26 October, 25 December, 26 December 2026.

sources.title: Nevada Revised Statutes 236.015, Legal holidays; closing of state, county and city offices, courts, public schools and Nevada System of Higher Education
sources.said: 1. The following days are declared to be legal holidays for state, county and city governmental offices: January 1 (New Year's Day); Martin Luther King, Jr.'s birthday ... observed on the third Monday in January; Washington's birthday ... observed on the third Monday in February; Last Monday in May (Memorial Day); June 19 (Juneteenth Day); July 4 (Independence Day); First Monday in September (Labor Day); Nevada Day is October 31 but is to be observed on the last Friday in October; November 11 (Veterans Day); Fourth Thursday in November (Thanksgiving Day); Friday following the fourth Thursday in November (Family Day); December 25 (Christmas Day). 2. ... all state, county and city offices, courts, public schools and the Nevada System of Higher Education must close on the legal holidays enumerated in subsection 1. 3. sources.said: § 24. Public holidays; half-holidays. The term public holiday includes the following days in each year: the first day of January, known as New Year's day; the third Monday of January, known as Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. day; the twelfth day of February, known as Lincoln's birthday; the third Monday in February, known as Washington's birthday; the last Monday in May, known as Memorial day; the second Sunday in June, known as Flag day (a Sunday, a day off already: not kept); the nineteenth day of June, known as Juneteenth; the fourth day of July, known as Independence day; the first Monday in September, known as Labor day; the second Monday in October, known as Columbus day; the eleventh day of November, known as Veterans' day; the fourth Thursday in November, known as Thanksgiving day; and the twenty-fifth day of December, known as Christmas day, and if any of such days except Flag day is Sunday, the next day thereafter; each general election day ...

sources.title: Code of Virginia § 2.2-3300. Legal holidays
sources.said: In each year, the following days are designated as legal holidays: January 1 — New Year's Day. The third Monday in January — Martin Luther King, Jr., Day. The second Monday in October — Columbus Day and Yorktown Victory Day. The Tuesday following the first Monday in November — Election Day. November 11 — Veterans Day. The fourth Thursday in November and the Friday next following — Thanksgiving Day. December 25 — Christmas Day. Whenever any of such days falls on Saturday, the Friday next preceding such day, or whenever any of such days falls on Sunday, the Monday next following such day.

entries.sought: Prince Edward Island’s paid holidays under its Employment Standards Act (in force June 30, 2026), and its rule for one on a day off

sources.title: Employment Standards Act (PEI, 2024, c.66), Legislative Counsel Office consolidation current to June 30, 2026
sources.said: s. 1(n) "paid holiday" means (i) New Year's Day, (ii) Islander Day, (iii) Good Friday, (iv) July 1, (v) Labour Day, (vi) National Day for Truth and Reconciliation, observed on September 30, (vii) Remembrance Day, (viii) Christmas Day, and (ix) any other day prescribed as a paid holiday. s. 27(2) Paid holiday not on work day: where a paid holiday falls on a day that is not a work day of an employee, the employer shall grant the employee a holiday with pay on (a) the employee's next work day immediately following the paid holiday; (b) the employee's next work day immediately following the employee's annual vacation; or (c) a day agreed upon by the employer and the employee that occurs before the employee's next annual vacation. (Its "July 1" is the day itself: the Act names no Sunday move, as the federal Holidays Act does for Canada Day.)

sources.said: 2(1) July 1, not being a Sunday, is a legal holiday and shall be kept and observed as such throughout Canada under the name of "Canada Day". sources.title: Canada Labour Code, s. 195, Substitution of general holidays
sources.said: An employer may, in respect of one or more employees subject to a collective agreement, substitute any other day for a general holiday if the substitution is agreed to in writing by the employer and the trade union; ... in respect of employees not subject to a collective agreement, if the substitution has been approved by that employee in writing, or by at least 70% of the affected employees.

sources.said: In New Brunswick and on Prince Edward Island, employment standards legislation does not designate a specific date for Canada Day, so when Canada Day falls on a Sunday, it will be observed on July 2nd, in accordance with the Holidays Act. In Nova Scotia and Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada Day is observed on July 1st, regardless of what day of the week it is.

Boxing Day (December 26, 2026) is a designated retail closing day.

sources.title: Government of Nova Scotia, Labour Standards, Holiday Pay
sources.said: When a paid holiday falls on a regular day off, the employer must give the employee a different day off with pay: the employer can decide that you would get your next scheduled work day off with pay, or an extra day off with pay added to your annual vacation, or you and your employer can agree on any other day off with pay.

sources.title: Government of Ontario, Your guide to the Employment Standards Act: Public holidays (last updated 2024-07-08)
sources.said: Ontario has nine public holidays: New Year's Day, Family Day, Good Friday, Victoria Day, Canada Day, Labour Day, Thanksgiving Day, Christmas Day, Boxing Day (December 26). If a public holiday falls on a day that is not ordinarily a working day for an employee, or during the employee's vacation, the employee is entitled to a substitute holiday off with public holiday pay, or public holiday pay for the public holiday if the employee agrees electronically or in writing. While some employers give their employees a holiday on Easter Sunday, Easter Monday, the first Monday in August, or Remembrance Day, the employer is not required to do so under the ESA.

sources.title: Government of the Northwest Territories, Education, Culture and Employment, Employment Standards: Frequently asked questions
sources.said: There are 11 statutory holidays in the Employment Standards Act. sources.title: Government of the Northwest Territories, Employment Standards Fact Sheet

sources.title: Fair Work Act 2009 (Cth), s. 115 (Compilation No. 73, 7 July 2026; authorised version C2026C00355)
sources.said: 115 (1) The following are public holidays: (a) each of these days: (i) 1 January (New Year’s Day); (ii) 26 January (Australia Day); (iii) Good Friday; (iv) Easter Monday; (v) 25 April (Anzac Day); (vi) the holiday for the birthday of the Sovereign (on the day on which it is celebrated in a State or Territory or a region of a State or Territory); (vii) 25 December (Christmas Day); (viii) 26 December (Boxing Day); (b) any other day, or part-day, declared or prescribed by or under a law of a State or Territory to be observed generally within the State or Territory, or a region of the State or Territory, as a public holiday. (2) If, under a law of a State or Territory, a day or part-day is substituted for a day or part-day that would otherwise be a public holiday because of subsection (1), then the substituted day or part-day is the public holiday.

sources.title: Holidays Act 1958 (ACT), s. 3, republication R11 (effective 1 January 2018; the current version, with the instruments made under it, ACT Legislation Register)
sources.said: 3 (1) (a) in any year each of the following days in that year is a public holiday in the ACT: (i) 1 January (New Year’s day), and, if that day falls on a Saturday or Sunday, the following Monday; (ii) 26 January (Australia Day), or, if that day falls on a Saturday or Sunday, the following Monday; (iii) the 2nd Monday in March (Canberra Day); (iv) Good Friday; (v) the Saturday following Good Friday; (vi) Easter Sunday; (vii) the Monday following Good Friday; (viii) 25 April (Anzac Day), or, if that day falls on a Sunday, the following Monday; (ix) 27 May (Reconciliation Day), or, if that day is not a Monday, the following Monday; (x) the 2nd Monday in June (the day for the observance of the anniversary of the birthday of the Sovereign); (xi) the 1st Monday in October (Labour Day); (xii) 25 December (Christmas Day) and— (A) if that day falls on a Saturday—the following Monday; or (B) if that day falls on a Sunday—the following Tuesday; (xiii) 26 December (Boxing Day) and— (A) if that day falls on a Saturday—the following Monday; or (B) if that day falls on a Sunday—the following Tuesday; and (b) any other day, or a part of any other day, that the Minister declares to be a public holiday in the ACT. Legislative instruments under the Act since 2022: Holidays (Anzac Day 2026) Declaration 2025 (No 1) NI2025-650 (repealed 25 March 2026); Holidays (Anzac Day Additional Public Holiday 2026) Declaration 2026 (No 1) NI2026-154; Holidays (Anzac Day Additional Public Holiday 2027) Declaration 2026 (No 1) NI2026-387.

sources.title: Statutory Holidays Act 2000 (Tas), s. 4 (authorised version as at 9 October 2026)
sources.said: 4. The following are statutory holidays to be observed as public holidays generally: (a) New Year’s Day (1 January), unless that day falls on a Saturday or Sunday, in which case the Monday following New Year’s Day; (b) Australia Day (26 January), unless that day falls on a Saturday or Sunday, in which case the following Monday; (c) the second Monday in March, known as Eight Hours Day or Labour Day; (d) Good Friday; (da) Easter Sunday; (e) Easter Monday; (g) Anzac Day (25 April); (h) the second Monday in June, for the anniversary of the birthday of the Sovereign; (i) Christmas Day (25 December); (ia) if Christmas Day falls on a Saturday, the Monday following Christmas Day; (ib) if Christmas Day falls on a Sunday, the Tuesday following Christmas Day; (j) Boxing Day (26 December), unless that day falls on a Saturday or Sunday, in which case – (i) the Monday following Boxing Day, if that day falls on a Saturday; or (ii) the Tuesday following Boxing Day, if that day falls on a Sunday. 5. Local statutory holidays: the days specified in column 1 of Part 1 of Schedule 1 for the areas of the State specified in column 3. 6. Easter Tuesday to be observed by certain persons: a person who is a member of a class of persons referred to in section 6 of the Industrial Relations (Commonwealth Powers) Act 2009.

sources.title: Government of Western Australia, Public holidays in Western Australia - 2026 to 2027 (the Public and Bank Holidays Act 1972)
sources.said: New Year's Day Thursday 1 January, Friday 1 January; Australia Day Monday 26 January, Tuesday 26 January; Labour Day Monday 2 March, Monday 1 March; Good Friday Friday 3 April, Friday 26 March; Easter Sunday Sunday 5 April, Sunday 28 March; Easter Monday Monday 6 April, Monday 29 March; Anzac Day Saturday 25 April & Monday 27 April, Sunday 25 April & Monday 26 April; Western Australia Day Monday 1 June, Monday 7 June; King's Birthday Monday 28 September, Monday 27 September; Christmas Day Friday 25 December, Saturday 25 December & Monday 27 December; Boxing Day Saturday 26 December & Monday 28 December, Sunday 26 December & Tuesday 28 December. When New Year’s Day, Anzac Day, or Christmas Day falls on a Saturday or Sunday the next following Monday is also a public holiday. When 26 January (Australia Day) falls on a Saturday or Sunday, the first Monday following 26 January is the public holiday. When Boxing Day falls on a Saturday the next following Monday is also a public holiday, and when Boxing Day falls on a Sunday or Monday the next following Tuesday is also a public holiday. Some regional areas in Western Australia hold the King's Birthday public holiday on an alternative date: City of Karratha Monday 3 August; Town of Port Hedland Monday 3 August.

sources.title: 全国年节及纪念日放假办法（根据2024年11月10日《国务院关于修改〈全国年节及纪念日放假办法〉的决定》第四次修订；国务院令第795号，新华社受权发布）
sources.said: 第二条 全体公民放假的节日：（一）元旦，放假1天（1月1日）；（二）春节，放假4天（农历除夕、正月初一至初三）；（三）清明节，放假1天（农历清明当日）；（四）劳动节，放假2天（5月1日、2日）；（五）端午节，放假1天（农历端午当日）；（六）中秋节，放假1天（农历中秋当日）；（七）国庆节，放假3天（10月1日至3日）。第三条 部分公民放假的节日及纪念日：（一）妇女节（3月8日），妇女放假半天；（二）青年节（5月4日），14周岁以上的青年放假半天；（三）儿童节（6月1日），不满14周岁的少年儿童放假1天；（四）中国人民解放军建军纪念日（8月1日），现役军人放假半天。第四条 少数民族习惯的节日，由各少数民族聚居地区的地方人民政府，按照各该民族习惯，规定放假日期。第六条 全体公民放假的假日，如果适逢周六、周日，应当在工作日补假。部分公民放假的假日，如果适逢周六、周日，则不补假。第七条 全体公民放假的假日，可合理安排统一放假调休，结合落实带薪年休假等制度，实际形成较长假期。

sources.title: Ratopati, Nepal’s Home Ministry Announces Eid-ul-Fitr Holiday on Saturday (March 20, 2026)
sources.said: The Ministry of Home Affairs has announced that the great festival of Muslims, Eid (Eid-ul-Fitr), will fall on Saturday. The ministry's statement mentioned the provision for a public holiday on the day of Eid as per the notice published in the Nepal Gazette.

sources.title: Décret n° 96-205 du 7 mars 1996 déterminant la liste et le régime des jours fériés (loidici.biz’s copy; the Journal officiel’s is not reachable here)
sources.said: ARTICLE PREMIER Conformément à l’article 24.2 du Code du Travail, le jour de la Fête nationale et le 1er mai, Fête du Travail sont jours fériés chômés et payés.

sources.title: Décret n° 2011-371 du 4 novembre 2011 modifiant et complétant l’article 2 du décret n° 96-205 du 7 mars 1996 (loidici.biz’s copy)
sources.said: ARTICLE 2 (NOUVEAU) Sauf dispositions conventionnelles plus favorables, sont fériés et chômés les jours de fêtes civiles ou religieuses dont la liste est établie ci-après : 1°) la fête du 1er janvier ; 2°) le lundi de Pâques ; 3°) le jour de l’Ascension ; 4°) le lundi de la Pentecôte ; 5°) la fête de fin du Ramadan (Ald-El-Fitr) ; 6°) la fête de la Tabaski (Aîd-El-Kébir) ; 7°) le 15 août, fête de l’Assomption ; 8°) le 1er novembre, fête de Toussaint ; 9°) le 15 novembre, Journée nationale de la Paix ; 10°) le 25 décembre, fête de Noël ; 11°) le lendemain de la Nuit du Destin (Lailatou-Kadr) ; 12°) le lendemain de l’anniversaire de la naissance du Prophète Mahomet (Maouloud) ; 13°) le lendemain de la fête nationale ou de la fête du travail chaque fois que lesdites fêtes tombent un dimanche ; 14°) le lendemain de la fête du Ramadan, chaque fois que ladite fête tombe un dimanche ; 15°) le lendemain de la fête de Noël, chaque fois que ladite fête tombe un dimanche ; 16°) le lendemain de la fête de Tabaski, chaque fois que ladite fête tombe un dimanche.

sources.title: Fraternité Matin, Nuit du destin 2026 : le lundi 16 mars 2026 déclaré jour férié et chômé en Côte d’Ivoire
sources.said: Le lundi 16 mars 2026 sera jour férié et chômé sur toute l’étendue du territoire national en Côte d’Ivoire. L’annonce a été faite à travers un communiqué signé le 12 mars 2026 par le ministre de l’Emploi, de la Protection sociale et de la Formation professionnelle, Adama Kamara. ... en application du décret n°2011-371 du 4 novembre 2011 ... le lundi 16 mars 2026, correspondant au lendemain de la Nuit du destin (Laylatoul-Kadr).

sources.title: Fraternité Matin, Aïd el-Fitr 2026 : le vendredi 20 mars déclaré jour férié et chômé en Côte d’Ivoire (19 mars 2026)
sources.said: Le gouvernement ivoirien a officiellement déclaré le vendredi 20 mars 2026 jour férié, chômé et payé sur toute l’étendue du territoire national, à l’occasion de la célébration de la fête de fin du Ramadan, communément appelée Aïd-El-Fitr. L’annonce a été faite à travers un communiqué du ministère de l’Emploi, de la Protection sociale et de la Formation professionnelle, en date du 18 mars 2026.

sources.title: Fraternité Matin, Tabaski 2026 : le COSIM et le CODISS annoncent la célébration le mercredi 27 mai en Côte d’Ivoire (21 mai 2026)
sources.said: la station à Arafat aura lieu, incha’Allah, le mardi 26 mai 2026. Par conséquent, la célébration de l’Aïd el-Kébir, communément appelée Tabaski en Côte d’Ivoire, interviendra le mercredi 27 mai 2026, correspondant au 10 Zoul-Hijja 1447 de l’Hégire.

sources.title: Agence Ivoirienne de Presse, Le Maouloud 2026 célébré dans la nuit du lundi au mardi, le 25 août déclaré jour férié et chômé (21 août 2026)
sources.said: Le ministre de l’Emploi, de la Protection sociale et de la Formation professionnelle a déclaré, dans un communiqué publié vendredi 21 août 2026, le mardi 25 août 2026 jour férié et chômé sur toute l’étendue du territoire national, au lendemain de la commémoration du Maouloud. Le Maouloud 2026 sera célébré dans la nuit du lundi 24 au mardi 25 août 2026.

sources.said: los días festivos que, de acuerdo con el Artículo 2.05 de la Ley 26-2017, según enmendada, conocida como "Ley de Cumplimiento con el Plan Fiscal", los empleados públicos de la Rama Ejecutiva disfrutarán como feriados de enero a diciembre de 2027: 1 de enero (viernes) Día de Año Nuevo; 6 de enero (miércoles) Día de Reyes; 18 de enero (tercer lunes de enero) Natalicio del Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr.; 15 de febrero (tercer lunes de febrero) Día de George Washington, Día de los Presidentes y el Día de las Mujeres y Hombres Próceres de Puerto Rico; 2 de marzo (martes) Día de la Ciudadanía Americana; 22 de marzo (lunes) Día de la Abolición de la Esclavitud; 26 de marzo (viernes) Viernes Santo; 31 de mayo (último lunes de mayo) Día de la Conmemoración de los Muertos en la Guerra (Memorial Day); 19 de junio (sábado) "Juneteenth National Independence Day"; 4 de julio (domingo) Día de la Independencia de los Estados Unidos [6]; 25 de julio (domingo) Día de la Constitución de Puerto Rico [7]; 27 de julio (martes) Día de José Celso Barbosa; 6 de septiembre (primer lunes de septiembre) Día del Trabajo; 11 de octubre (segundo lunes de octubre) Día de la Raza (Descubrimiento de América); 11 de noviembre (jueves) Día del Veterano; 19 de noviembre (viernes) Día de la Puertorriqueñidad; 25 de noviembre (cuarto jueves de noviembre) Día de Acción de Gracias; 25 de diciembre (sábado) Día de Navidad. sources.title: Republic of Kiribati, Public Holidays Ordinance (Cap. 81) (Section 6, 9), Order (Alteration of days appointed to be public holidays), 18 December 2025 (Office of Te Beretitenti, Gazettes & Instruments: National Public Holiday 2026; scanned, read as images)
sources.said: IN EXERCISE of the powers conferred upon me by section 6 of the Public Holidays Ordinance (Cap. 81), I hereby declare the following days to be public holidays for 2026. Thursday, 1st January New Year’s Day; Friday, 2nd January Kiribati Holiday; Monday, 9th March In honour of International Women’s Day; Friday, 3rd April Good Friday; Monday 6th April Easter Monday; Tuesday, 7th April National Health Day; Friday, 1st May International Labour Day; Monday, 22nd June In honour of National Police Day; Friday, 10th July Gospel Day; Monday 13th July In honour of National Day; Tuesday 14th July Kiribati Culture and Senior Citizens Day; Wednesday, 15th July Kiribati Special Day; Monday, 3rd August National Youth & Children’s Day; Monday, 5th October World Teachers Day; Friday 11th December In honour of Human Rights Day; Friday, 25th December Christmas Day; Monday, 28th December In honour of Boxing Day (Gift Day); Tuesday 29th December Kiribati Holiday; Wednesday 30th December Kiribati Holiday; Thursday 31st December Kiribati Holiday. I further declare that any day appointed to be a public holiday under section 2 of the Ordinance that does not appear in the list above shall be a public holiday in 2026. Dated this 18th day of December, 2025. TANETI MAAMAU, BERETITENTI.

sources.title: States of Guernsey, Public holiday dates (2026 and 2027; the Public Holidays Ordinance, 2009)
sources.said: The statutory public holidays for 2026 are as follows: Thursday 1st January New Year's Day; Friday 3rd April Good Friday; Monday 6th April Easter Monday; Monday 4th May May Day bank holiday; Saturday 9th May Liberation Day; Monday 25th May Spring bank holiday; Monday 31st August Summer bank holiday; Friday 25th December Christmas Day; Monday 28th December Boxing Day (substitute day). 2027: Friday 1st January New Year's Day; Friday 26th March Good Friday; Monday 29th March Easter Monday; Monday 3th May May Day bank holiday; Sunday 9th May Liberation Day; Monday 31st May Spring bank holiday; Monday 30th August Summer bank holiday; Monday 27th December Christmas Day (substitute day); Tuesday 28th December Boxing Day (substitute day). All public holidays are prescribed by the Public Holidays Ordinance, 2009 as follows: New Year's Day, if a weekday; the 2nd January, in a year when New Year's Day falls on a Sunday; the 3rd January, in a year where New Year's Day falls on a Saturday; Easter Monday; the first Monday in May; the 9th May, Liberation Day; the last Monday in May; the last Monday in August; the 26th December, Boxing Day, if a weekday; the 27th December, in a year when Christmas Day or Boxing Day falls on a Sunday; the 28th December, in a year where Christmas Day or Boxing Day falls on a Saturday. "Weekday" does not include a Saturday. Christmas Day and Good Friday (and all Sundays) are customary la[w holidays].

sources.said: Нерабочими праздничными днями в Российской Федерации являются: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 и 8 января - Новогодние каникулы; 7 января - Рождество Христово; 23 февраля - День защитника Отечества; 8 марта - Международный женский день; 1 мая - Праздник Весны и Труда; 9 мая - День Победы; 12 июня - День России; 4 ноября - День народного единства. При совпадении выходного и нерабочего праздничного дней выходной день переносится на следующий после праздничного рабочий день, за исключением выходных дней, совпадающих с нерабочими праздничными днями, указанными в абзацах втором и третьем части первой настоящей статьи. Правительство Российской Федерации переносит два выходных дня из числа выходных дней, совпадающих с нерабочими праздничными днями, указанными в абзацах втором и третьем части первой настоящей статьи, на другие дни в очередном календарном году.

sources.title: Ley 27.399, Establecimiento de feriados y fines de semana largos (B.O. 18/10/2017; argentina.gob.ar, texto)
sources.said: ARTÍCULO 1°.- Establécense como días feriados nacionales y días no laborables en todo el territorio de la Nación los siguientes: FERIADOS NACIONALES INAMOVIBLES: 1° de enero: Año Nuevo. Lunes y Martes de Carnaval. 24 de marzo: Día Nacional de la Memoria por la Verdad y la Justicia. Viernes Santo. 2 de abril: Día del Veterano y de los Caídos en la Guerra de Malvinas. 1° de mayo: Día del Trabajo. 25 de mayo: Día de la Revolución de Mayo. 20 de junio: Paso a la Inmortalidad del General Don Manuel Belgrano. 9 de julio: Día de la Independencia. 8 de diciembre: Día de la Inmaculada Concepción de María. 25 de diciembre: Navidad. FERIADOS NACIONALES TRASLADABLES: 17 de junio: Paso a la Inmortalidad del General Don Martín Miguel de Güemes. 17 de agosto: Paso a la Inmortalidad del General Don José de San Martín. 12 de octubre: Día del Respeto a la Diversidad Cultural. 20 de noviembre: Día de la Soberanía Nacional. DIAS NO LABORABLES: Jueves Santo. … ARTÍCULO 6°.- Los feriados nacionales trasladables establecidos por el artículo 1° de la presente cuyas fechas coincidan con los días martes y miércoles serán trasladados al día lunes anterior. Los que coincidan con los días jueves y viernes serán trasladados al día lunes siguiente. ARTÍCULO 7°.- El Poder Ejecutivo nacional podrá, adicionalmente a lo establecido en el artículo anterior, fijar anualmente hasta tres (3) días feriados o no laborables destinados a promover la actividad turística, que deberán coincidir con los días lunes o viernes.

sources.title: Decreto 1103/2026 (DNU), visita oficial de Su Santidad el Papa León XIV (argentina.gob.ar, texto)
sources.said: ARTÍCULO 2°.- Establécese como feriado nacional el día lunes 9 de noviembre de 2026 en todo el territorio de la REPÚBLICA ARGENTINA, con motivo de la visita de Su Santidad el Papa LEÓN XIV. ARTÍCULO 3°.- Establécese como feriado el día martes 10 de noviembre de 2026, exclusivamente en el ámbito de la Provincia de CÓRDOBA y la CIUDAD AUTÓNOMA DE BUENOS AIRES, con motivo de la visita de Su Santidad el Papa LEÓN XIV. ARTÍCULO 4°.- Establécese como feriado el día miércoles 11 de noviembre de 2026, exclusivamente en el ámbito de la Provincia de BUENOS AIRES, con motivo de la visita de Su Santidad el Papa LEÓN XIV.

sources.title: Ley Nº 7544/2025, que determina los feriados nacionales de la República del Paraguay, se establecen los feriados móviles y se faculta al Poder Ejecutivo a instituir otros feriados en situaciones especiales (Biblioteca y Archivo Central del Congreso Nacional)
sources.said: Artículo 1º.- De los Feriados Nacionales. Determínase como días Feriados Nacionales de la República del Paraguay de cada año, además de los días domingos, los siguientes: • 1 de enero, Año Nuevo. • 1 de marzo, Día de los Héroes de la Patria. • Jueves y Viernes, Semana Santa. • 1 de mayo, Día de los Trabajadores. • 14 y 15 de mayo, Día de la Independencia Nacional. • 12 de junio, Día de la Paz del Chaco. • 20 de junio, Día de la Jura de la Constitución Nacional. • 15 de agosto, Día de la Fundación de Asunción y eventualmente, Día de Transmisión del Mando Presidencial. • 29 de setiembre, Día de la Batalla de Boquerón. • 8 de diciembre, Día de la Virgen de Caacupé. • 25 de diciembre, Día de la Navidad. Artículo 2º.- Feriados Móviles. Establecer como Feriados Móviles, que podrán ser trasladados por el Poder Ejecutivo, los siguientes: • 1 de marzo … • 12 de junio … • 20 de junio … • 29 de setiembre … Artículo 3º.- Traslado de feriados a los días lunes. Autorízase al Poder Ejecutivo a trasladar anualmente, por Decreto, los Feriados Nacionales mencionados en el artículo 2° de la presente ley, a los días lunes, anterior o siguiente al feriado que se traslada. Artículo 4º.- Feriados adicionales. Facúltase al Poder Ejecutivo a fijar cada año, por Decreto, hasta un máximo de tres días adicionales de Feriados Nacionales … Artículo 7º.- Asuetos. … Los asuetos serán considerados días hábiles y no tendrán los efectos de los Feriados Nacionales

Član 3b Izuzetno od člana 2 i člana 3 st. 2 i 3 ovog zakona, praznik 13. novembar - Njegošev dan, crnogorski praznik kulture, praznuje se jedan dan i to na dan praznika.

sources.title: Закон Республики Казахстан от 13 декабря 2001 года № 267-II «О праздниках в Республике Казахстан» (с изменениями по Закону РК от 11.06.2026 № 306-VIII, вводится в действие с 01.07.2026; ИПС «Әділет»)
sources.said: Статья 2. Национальные праздники Национальным праздником в Республике Казахстан является День Республики Казахстан, отмечаемый 25 октября. … Статья 3. Государственные праздники Государственными праздниками в Республике Казахстан являются праздники, отмечаемые в следующие дни: Новый год - 1-2 января; Международный женский день - 8 марта; День Конституции Республики Казахстан – 15 марта; Наурыз мейрамы - 21-23 марта; Праздник единства народа Казахстана - 1 мая; День защитника Отечества - 7 мая; День Победы - 9 мая; День Столицы - 6 июля; День Независимости – 16 декабря. … Статья 5. Праздничные дни … Праздничные дни в Республике Казахстан являются нерабочими днями. При совпадении выходного и праздничного дней выходным днем является следующий после праздничного рабочий день.

sources.title: Трудовой кодекс Республики Казахстан от 23 ноября 2015 года № 414-V, статья 84 (ИПС «Әділет»)
sources.said: 5. Первый день Курбан-айта, отмечаемого по мусульманскому календарю, 7 января – православное Рождество являются выходными днями независимо от применяемых режимов работы и графиков сменности (графикам вахт).

sources.title: Informburo.kz, Переносы выходных и Курбан-айт в мае: календарь праздничных дней в Казахстане на 2026 год (January 2026), from the e-government portal's calendar
sources.said: В январе – 3 (отмечаемые в эти дни новогодние праздники и Рождество). В марте – 4. Международный женский день в 2026 году выпадет на воскресенье, поэтому казахстанцы отдохнут 9 марта, в понедельник. Два из трёх дней празднования Наурыза (21 и 22 марта) также выпадают на субботу и воскресенье, поэтому 24 и 25 марта будут выходными днями. Таким образом, казахстанцы дополнительно отдохнут 9, 23, 24, 25 марта. В мае – 4. … В 2026 году первый день Курбан-айта приходится на 27 мая. 9 мая выпадает на субботу, поэтому выходным днём будет 11 мая (понедельник). В июле – 1 (День столицы – 6 июля). … В октябре – 1. День Республики, отмечаемый 25 октября, выпадает на воскресенье, поэтому дополнительным выходным будет понедельник, 26 октября. В декабре – 1 (День Независимости – 16 декабря).

sources.said: January 1; Constitution Day, January 7; Independence Day, March 6; Good Friday, April 18 and Easter Monday, April 21. sources.title: Ghana News Agency, Parliament restores July 1 as Republic Day holiday (25 June 2025): the Amendment Act, 2025 (Act 1142, assented and commenced 30 June 2025)
sources.said: The newly passed legislation restored July 1 as Republic Day, formally recognising the country’s transition to a republic in 1960. It also introduced a new public holiday for the Muslim community, known as Shaqq Day, to be observed a day after Eid-ul-Fitr. … The bill also repealed August 4 as Founders’ Day and reinstated September 21 as Founder’s Day in honour of Dr. Kwame Nkrumah … Further, the bill empowered the President to shift public holidays that fell on Tuesdays, Wednesdays, or Thursdays to either the preceding Friday or following Monday

sources.said: 2. The several days mentioned in the Schedule and such other special day or days as may be appointed under section 7 are hereby declared to be "Public General Holidays". … SCHEDULE 1. New Year’s Day, or in case New Year’s Day falls on Sunday, then the day after New Year’s Day. 2. Ash Wednesday. 3. Easter Monday. 4. The 23rd day of May (or in case the 23rd day of May falls on Saturday or Sunday, then the following Monday) which shall be known as "National Labour Day". 5. The following days in August, that is to say— (a) the 1st day of August (or in case the 1st day of August falls on a Sunday, then the following Monday) which shall be known as "Emancipation Day"; (b) the 6th day of August (or in case the 6th day of August falls on a Sunday, then the following Monday) which shall be known as "Independence Day". 6. The third Monday in the month of October, which shall be known as "National Heroes’ Day". 7. The day after Christmas Day, or when Christmas Day falls on a Sunday, then the 26th and 27th of December. 8. A day appointed by the Minister of national observance.

sources.title: Jamaica Gleaner, Legal Scoop: When a public holiday falls on a Saturday (Shena Stubbs-Gibson, 12 January 2020)
sources.said: The Holidays (Public General) Act (the act) sets out the public holidays that are observed in Jamaica and how to treat them, in the event any falls on a weekend. Since certain holidays, such as Good Friday, Easter Monday, Ash Wednesday and National Heroes Day, occur on the same day each year, it is only New Year’s Day, Labour Day, Independence Day, Emancipation Day, Christmas Day and Boxing Day which are likely to fall on a weekend. … However, since the act makes no similar provision for those instances where these holidays fall on a Saturday, where that occurs, they are to be celebrated on the said Saturday. … However, if Christmas Day falls on a Saturday, Boxing Day will then fall on a Sunday, it will not move to the Monday as Boxing Day is always the day after Christmas Day.

sources.said: 1. Azərbaycan Respublikasının bayram günlərinə aşağıdakılar aiddir: Yeni il bayramı (1 və 2 yanvar); Qadınlar günü (8 mart); Faşizm üzərində qələbə günü (9 may); Respublika günü (28 may); Azərbaycan xalqının milli qurtuluş günü (15 iyun); Azərbaycan Respublikasının Silahlı Qüvvələri günü (26 iyun); Dövlət müstəqiliyi günü (18 oktyabr); Azərbaycan Respublikasının Dövlət Bayrağı günü (9 noyabr); Konstitusiya günü (12 noyabr); Milli Dirçəliş günü (17 noyabr); Dünya azərbaycanlılarının həmrəyliyi günü (31 dekabr); Novruz bayramı – 5 gün; Qurban bayramı – 2 gün. Ramazan bayramı – 2 gün. 2. Yeni il bayramı, Qadınlar günü, Faşizm üzərində qələbə günü, Azərbaycan xalqının milli qurtuluş günü, Azərbaycan Respublikasının Silahlı Qüvvələri günü, Azərbaycan Respublikası Dövlət Bayrağı günü, Dünya azərbaycanlılarının həmrəyliyi günü, Novruz bayramı, Qurban bayramı və Ramazan bayramı iş günü hesab edilmir. … 4. sources.title: ilex.by (ООО «ЮрСпектр»), Переносы рабочих дней и длинные выходные в Беларуси: как отдыхаем в 2026 году (23.07.2025)
sources.said: Согласно постановлению от 22.07.2025 № 397 в 2026 году рабочий день 20 апреля (понедельник) переносится на 25 апреля (суббота). Нерабочими будут 4 дня подряд: 18 (суббота), 19 (воскресенье), 20 (понедельник) и 21 (вторник) апреля. Переносы в 2026 году, как и ранее, распространяются только на работников, которые работают в условиях пятидневной рабочей недели и для которых суббота и воскресенье – выходные. … Нерабочие (праздничные) дни в 2026 году : 1 и 2 января – Новый год; 7 января – Рождество Христово (православное Рождество); 8 марта – День женщин; 21 апреля – Радуница по календарю православной конфессии; 1 мая – Праздник труда; 9 мая – День Победы; 3 июля – День Независимости (День Республики); 7 ноября – День Октябрьской революции; 25 декабря – Рождество Христово (католическое Рождество).

sources.title: Трудовой кодекс Туркменистана (Меджлис Туркменистана, consolidated), статья 81
sources.said: Статья 81. Праздничные и памятные дни 1. Работа на предприятиях, в организациях и учреждениях не производится в следующие всенародные праздничные и памятные дни: 1) Новый год – 1 января; 2) Международный женский день – 8 марта; 3) Национальный праздник весны – 21-22 марта; 4) День Конституции Туркменистана и Государственного флага Туркменистана – 18 мая; 5) День независимости Туркменистана – 27 сентября; 6) День поминовения – 6 октября; 7) Международный день Нейтралитета – 12 декабря; 8) Курбан байрамы – конкретная дата Курбан байрамы ежегодно определяется Указом Президента Туркменистана; 9) Ораза байрамы – конкретная дата Ораза байрамы ежегодно определяется Указом Президента Туркменистана. … 2. При совпадении нерабочих праздничного или памятного дня с выходным днём (воскресенье) выходным днём является следующий после праздничного или памятного дня рабочий день.

sources.title: Confederația Națională a Sindicatelor din Moldova, Care sunt zilele de sărbătoare nelucrătoare în Republica Moldova? (the Labour Code, art. 111)
sources.said: În Republica Moldova zile de sărbătoare nelucrătoare sunt: a) 1 ianuarie – Anul Nou; b) 7 și 8 ianuarie – Nașterea lui Isus Hristos (Crăciunul pe stil vechi); c) 8 martie – Ziua internațională a femeii; d) prima și a doua zi de Paște conform calendarului bisericesc; e) ziua de luni la o săptămână după Paște (Paștele Blajinilor); f) 1 mai – Ziua internațională a solidarității oamenilor muncii; g) 9 mai – Ziua Victoriei și a comemorării eroilor căzuți pentru independența Patriei; h) 9 mai – Ziua Europei; i) 27 august – Ziua Independenței; j) 31 august – sărbătoarea “Limba noastră”; k) 25 decembrie – Nașterea lui Iisus Hristos (Crăciunul pe stil nou); l) ziua Hramului bisericii din localitatea respectivă, declarată în modul stabilit de consiliul local al municipiului, orașului, comunei, satului.

sources.title: #diez, Câte zile libere vor avea moldovenii în anul 2026. Lista sărbătorilor în Moldova (Petru Beșleaga, 1 ianuarie 2026)
sources.said: Conform legislației, în Moldova sunt 13 sărbători oficiale … # 1 ianuarie – Anul Nou (joi); # 7 ianuarie – Crăciunul pe stil vechi (miercuri); # 8 ianuarie – a doua zi de Crăciun pe stil vechi (joi); # 8 martie – Ziua Internațională a Femeii (duminică); # 12 aprilie – prima zi de Paște (duminică); # 13 aprilie – a doua zi de Paște (luni); # 20 aprilie – Paștele Blajinilor (luni); # 1 mai – Ziua Muncii (vineri); # 9 mai – Ziua Europei și Ziua Comemorării victimelor Celui de-Al Doilea Război Mondial (sâmbătă); # 1 iunie – Ziua Copilului (luni); # 27 august – Ziua Independenței (joi); # 31 august – Ziua Națională „Limba Noastră” (luni); # 25 decembrie – Crăciunul pe stil nou (vineri).

sources.title: Radio Moldova, Zilele de sărbătoare nelucrătoare din 2026: trei sunt în weekend
sources.said: În schimb, unele sărbători importante, precum Ziua Internațională a Femeii (8 martie) și Ziua Europei (9 mai) vor fi marcate în zile de weekend, fără a genera zile libere suplimentare pentru salariați. … Ziua Muncii: 1 mai (vineri); Ziua Copilului: 1 iunie (luni); Sărbătoarea „Limba Noastră”: 31 august (luni); Crăciunul pe stil nou: 25 decembrie (vineri). sources.title: Presidential Order No. 54 of 2017 determining Official Public Holidays (Official Gazette 11 of 13 March 2017; RwandaLII, "the latest version")
sources.said: Article 2 – Scope of application This Order applies to all employees and employers in the public and private sector. Article 3 – Official public holidays Official public holidays in the public and private sector are as follows: 1° 01 January: New Year’s day; 2° 02 January: Day after New Year’s Day; 3° 01 February: National Heroes’ Day; 4° Good Friday; 5° Easter Monday; 6° 07 April: Genocide perpetrated against the Tutsi Memorial Day; 7° 01 May: Labour Day; 8° 01 July: Independence Day; 9° 04 July: Liberation Day; 10° Friday of the first week of August: Umuganura Day; 11° 15 August: Assumption Day; 12° 25 December: Christmas Day; 13° 26 December: Boxing Day; 14° EID EL FITR: the date is announced each year by Rwanda Moslems’ Association; 15° EID AL-ADHA: the date is announced each year by Rwanda Moslems’ Association. Article 4 – Coincidence of official public holidays with weekend days Except 07 April, Genocide perpetrated against the Tutsi Memorial Day, if an official public holiday falls on weekend, the following working day becomes an official public holiday. If two (2) consecutive official public holidays fall on weekend, the two (2) official public holidays are compensated in one (1) working day that follows. In case of coincidence of two (2) official public holidays, the following working day becomes an official public holiday to compensate one (1) of the two (2) coinciding public holidays.

sources.title: Loi n° 74-52 du 4 novembre 1974 relative à la fête nationale et aux fêtes légales (legislative file, Direction des relations avec les institutions, through vie-publique.sn; the scan’s text-layer typing slips corrected)
sources.said: Article premier. - La République célèbre le quatre avril comme jour de fête nationale. Art. 2. - Outre la fête nationale et outre les fêtes de Pâques et de Pentecôte tombant un dimanche, les fêtes suivantes sont fêtes légales: Premier janvier ; Premier mai; Journée du Mawloud; Journée de la Korité; Journée de Tabaski ; Lundi de Pâques; Jeudi de l'Ascension; Lundi de la Pentecôte; Journée du 15 août; Journée de la Toussaint; Vingt-cinq décembre. Quand la Korité et la Tabaski tombent un dimanche, le lundi suivant est férié. Art. 3. - Les fêtes légales sont chômées. … la fête religieuse du Mawloud se composant traditionnellement de la nuit du Mawloud proprement dit et de la journée qui suit, il est inutile de préciser au 2° alinéa de l'article que, lorsque le Mawloud tombe un dimanche, le lundi suivant est férié.

sources.title: Burkina24, Burkina Faso : Le pays réduit le nombre de jours chômés et payés de 15 à 11 (9 janvier 2026)
sources.said: Avec cette réforme, le Burkina Faso passe de 15 à 11 jours chômés et payés. Il s’agit notamment du 1er janvier (jour de l’An), du 8 mars (Journée internationale des droits de la femme), du 1er mai (Fête du travail), du 15 mai (Journée des coutumes et des traditions), du 15 août (Assomption), du 11 décembre (Fête nationale), du 25 décembre (Noël), ainsi que des fêtes mobiles que sont l’Ascension, le Mouloud, le Ramadan et la Tabaski. Par ailleurs, certains jours autrefois fériés et payés deviennent désormais des journées de commémoration et de recueillement. Il s’agit du 3 janvier (soulèvement populaire), du 4 août (avènement de la Révolution populaire et démocratique), du 5 août (proclamation de l’indépendance), du 15 octobre (commémoration de l’assassinat du Président Isidore Noël Thomas Sankara), du 31 octobre (Journée nationale des martyrs) et du 1er novembre (Fête de l’armée et Toussaint). Le ministre en charge de la Fonction publique, Mathias Traoré, a indiqué que l’adoption de cette loi abroge immédiatement celle de 2015 qui instituait les fêtes légales et les événements à caractère historique. … Selon Mathias Traoré, désormais, lorsqu’une fête tombe un dimanche, le lendemain ne sera plus automatiquement déclaré chômé.

Cette décision s’inscrit dans le cadre de l’application de la loi n°001-2026/ALT du 09 janvier 2026

sources.title: WageIndicator Mali, Congé annuel et vacances (mis à jour le 2026-03-30)
sources.said: Les jours fériés au Mali sont régis par la loi du travail 05-040 du 22 juillet 2005. Cette loi combine toutes les autres lois sous le code du travail et établit ces 12 jours fériés officiels. Cette dernière donne également au gouvernement le pouvoir d'établir des fêtes nationales ponctuelles tout au long de l'année si l'occasion se présente. … 1er janvier - Jour de l’année ; 20 janvier - Journée des forces armées ; 26 mars - Jour des martyrs/Jour de la démocratie; 22 avril - lundi de Pâques ; 1er mai - Fête du travail ; 25 mai - Journée de l'Afrique ; 5 juin – Korité/Fin du Ramadhan ; 12 août – Tabaski/Fête du Sacrifice ; 22 septembre - Jour de l'indépendance ; 10 novembre - Anniversaire du prophète Mahomet ; 17 novembre - Baptême du prophète et 25 décembre - le jour de Noël. Les jours fériés qui tombent un dimanche sont déplacés au lendemain c’est-à -dire le lundi suivant. Les vacances qui se produisent un samedi restent à cette date. … Source: Articles 1-3 de la Loi N° 05-040 du 22 juillet 2005 relative aux fêtes légales en République du Mali.

entries.sought: Saint Kitts and Nevis's public holidays, the days off its law or its government's list names, nationally and in each first-level region that keeps its own

sources.title: Public Holidays Act, Cap. 23.23 (Revised Laws, revision date 31 December 2002), Schedule and s. 5
sources.said: The anniversary of the birth of the Sovereign or the day, of which due public notice shall be given, appointed to be kept as the Sovereign’s birthday. The first day of January in each year. Independence Day, being the 19th day of September. National Heroes Day, which shall be the 16th day of September. If any of the above-mentioned days fall on a Sunday the next following Monday shall be a public holiday. Boxing Day—that is the day after Christmas Day, but if Christmas Day falls on a Saturday, then the next following Monday shall be a public holiday, and if Christmas Day falls on a Sunday, then the next following Monday and Tuesday shall be public holidays. Easter Monday. Labour Day (the first Monday in May). Whit Monday. The first Monday in August, which shall be known as Emancipation Day. … Note: Sundays, Christmas Day and Good Friday are observed as Common Law Holidays. … 5. It shall be lawful for the Governor-General to issue a proclamation— (a) appointing a special day or part of a day to be reserved as a public holiday either throughout the State or in any island, town, district or village thereof

sources.title: Code of Canon Law, can. 1246 (vatican.va)
sources.said: Can. 1246 §1. Sunday, on which by apostolic tradition the paschal mystery is celebrated, must be observed in the universal Church as the primordial holy day of obligation. The following days must also be observed: the Nativity of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Epiphany, the Ascension, the Body and Blood of Christ, Holy Mary the Mother of God, her Immaculate Conception, her Assumption, Saint Joseph, Saint Peter and Saint Paul the Apostles, and All Saints. §2. With the prior approval of the Apostolic See, however, the conference of bishops can suppress some of the holy days of obligation or transfer them to a Sunday.

sources.said: The Schedule to the principal Act is repealed and replaced as follows – “SCHEDULE 1. NEW YEARS DAY The First day of January in each year When the First day of January falls on a Sunday the following Monday shall be a public holiday. 2. INDEPENDENCE DAY The first day of November in each year When the first day of November falls on a Saturday or Sunday the following Monday shall be a public holiday … 3. CHRISTMAS DAY … When the Twenty-fifth day of December falls on a Saturday or Sunday, the following Monday and Tuesday shall be public holidays. 4. BOXING DAY … When the Twenty-sixth day of December falls on a Sunday, the following Monday and Tuesday shall be public holidays. 5. GOOD FRIDAY 6. EASTER MONDAY 7. LABOUR DAY The First Monday in May 8. WHIT MONDAY 9. CARNIVAL HOLIDAY The First Monday in August The Tuesday following the First Monday in August 10. SIR VERE CORNWALL BIRD SNR. DAY The 9th day of December in each year When the Ninth day of December falls on a Saturday or Sunday, the following Monday shall be a public holiday. 11. THE DAY FOLLOWING A GENERAL ELECTION IN ANTIGUA AND BARBUDA 12. SUNDAY For the purpose of employment standards and labour relations, Section C14 (Public holiday leave) and C15 (Public holiday pay) of the Antigua and Barbuda Labour Code, Cap. 27 do not apply to Sundays, except one of the other public holiday falls on a Sunday.

entries.foundInPart: Kedah’s 2026 notice gives its rule: a state holiday on a Friday, or on another holiday, is replaced by the following day (and by the day after where that is a holiday already); one on a Saturday is a holiday and is not replaced. Read at the source (2026-11-02), the "following day" of a Friday is the Saturday, itself Kedah’s second day of weekly rest, and the notice names no day in place of 2026’s Friday holidays (1 May, 25 December): whether the day off falls on the Saturday or the Sunday is not settled by any source read, so Kedah’s replacement days stay unkept. Its added Hari Raya day (Monday 23 March 2026, by the State Secretary’s letter of 15 March 2026) is kept, in place of the Friday the Prime Minister gave elsewhere.

sources.said: Bagi Hari Kelepasan Am yang disenaraikan, sekiranya Hari Kelepasan Am jatuh pada Hari Kelepasan Mingguan (Jumaat dan Sabtu) secara berturut-turut, maka hari-hari itu diganti dengan hari esoknya (satu hari sahaja) dan jika kemudiannya pula sedia menjadi hari kelepasan, maka hari yang berikutnya dijadikan Hari Kelepasan Am. Apabila Hari Kelepasan Am jatuh pada hari pertama Kelepasan Mingguan (Hari Jumaat), tidak ada cuti gantian bagi Hari Kelepasan Am tersebut kecuali apabila Hari Kelepasan Am jatuh pada Hari Kedua (Hari Sabtu) maka hari berikutnya adalah hari cuti gantian. value.rule: A holiday on Friday, the first day of the weekly rest, has no day in its place; one on Saturday, the second, has the next day; Friday and Saturday holidays together have the next day only; and where that day is a holiday already, the day after it (the Arahan PSUK of 27 November 2025).
value.note: 2026-03-08 for Nuzul Al-Quran (Saturday 7 March) and 2026-03-23 for Hari Raya Puasa (Saturday 21 March; Sunday 22 March its second day), which the 18 March 2026 letter confirms was gazetted; 2027-02-08, 2027-05-02 and 2027-12-26 are the same rule applied to the federal 2027 table’s Saturday holidays in Kelantan (Tahun Baharu Cina 6 February, its second day Sunday 7 February; Hari Pekerja 1 May; Hari Krismas 25 December), before Kelantan’s own 2027 instruction is out.

sources.title: République de Madagascar, Décret n° 2026-006 du 08 janvier 2026 fixant la liste des jours fériés, chômés et payés au titre de l’année 2026 (CNLEGIS)
sources.said: Article premier : ... les journées ci-après sont déclarées fériées, chômées et payées, au titre de l’année 2026 : 1. Le jeudi 1er janvier : Jour de l'An 2. Le dimanche 08 mars : Journée internationale de la Femme, fériée et chômée uniquement pour les femmes 3. Le dimanche 29 mars : Journée commémorative des morts des évènements de 1947 4. Le dimanche 05 avril : Pâques 5. Le lundi 06 avril : Lundi de Pâques 6. Le vendredi 1er mai : Fête du Travail 7. Le jeudi 14 mai : Ascension 8. Le dimanche 24 mai : Pentecôte 9. Le lundi 25 mai : Lundi de Pentecôte 10. Le vendredi 26 juin : Fête nationale de l’Indépendance 11. Le samedi 15 août : Assomption 12. Le dimanche 1er novembre : Toussaint 13. Le vendredi 25 décembre : Noël. Article 2 : Sont également fériées, chômées et payées les journées respectives pour célébrer : - l’Eid Al- Fitr et l’Eid Al-Adha, suivant le calendrier fixé par la Communauté musulmane ; - le Nouvel An ou TAOMBAOVAO MALAGASY, suivant le calendrier fixé lors de la Concertation Nationale. Article 3 : Est également chômée et payée, la journée nationale de la culture dont la date est fixée par le Ministère de la Communication et de la Culture. Article 4 : Toute autre journée ... qui sera déclarée chômée et payée, doit faire l’objet d’un Décret publié une semaine à l’avance.

sources.said: A Lei nº 16/IV/91, de 30 de dezembro, determina que são feriados nacionais com total cessação de todas as atividades não permitidas por lei aos Domingos, as datas que indica no seu artigo 1º. entries.foundInPart: Progress: the law that names the national holidays is Lei n.º 16/IV/91, de 30 de dezembro (art. 1), with municipal days set by each Assembleia Municipal (art. 2, max two; Estatuto dos Municípios, Lei 134/IV/95, art. 81(1)(i)); Praia's is 29 April (Deliberação 16/2018). Its article 1 list and the other concelhos' days are still unread. Next: the BO's 1992 S1 issues beyond February, or later amending laws, could carry it. sources.title: Bollettino Ufficiale della Repubblica Democratica Somala, Anno IV, Suppl. n. 3 al n. 10, 25 October 1972: Law No. 65 of 18 October 1972, Labour Code (English text, p. 1114 on), Università Roma Tre, Archivio Leggi della Somalia (1950-1989), handle 2307/7374
sources.said: Article 86(2), proviso: 'work done on national and public holidays shall be paid as under: (a) 1st May (Labour day) - 1 day; 1st July (National Commorative day) - 1 day; 21st October (Revolution day - 1 day) [100% more]; (b) Idd-EL-Fitr - 2 days; Idd-El-Adha - 2 days; 26th June - 1 day; 12 Rabi-El-Awal (Birthday of Prophet - 1 day) [50% more]; (c) Other Public Holidays'. Article 96: '1. Every worker shall be entitled to one day's rest each week, which should normally fall on Friday ... 3. Workers shall also be entitled to a rest day on public holidays recognised as such by the State. 4. A worker shall be entitled to full remuneration on all national holidays in letters (a) and (b) of the proviso to paragraph 2 of Article 86'.

sources.title: Xeerka Lr. 65 ee 18 Octoobar 1972, Xeerka Shaqada (Somali text of the Labour Code), Università Roma Tre, Archivio Leggi della Somalia, handle 2307/26437
sources.said: Qodobka 86(5): 'a) 1 Maajo (Maalinka Shaqada) 1 maalin; 1 Juulay (Sanadguurada Gobannimada) hal maalin; 21 Oktoobar (Sanadguuradi Kacaanka) 2 maalin [100%]; b) Ciidil Fitri (2 maalin), Ciidul Adxa (2 maalin), 26 juun 1 malin, 12 Rabiicul Awala (Dhalashada Nabiga CS) 1 maalin [50%]; c) ciidaha kale Guud.' Qodobka 96(3): rest on 'maalmaha ciidaha qaranka, kuwaasoo ay dawladdu aqoonsantahay'. (The Somali text gives 21 October two days where the English gives one.)

entries.foundInPart: Partial. The law found is the 1972 Labour Code, which the press says a new Labour Code (2024-2026, 'Law No. 36' per one guide) has replaced; its holiday article is unread, so the 1972 list may no longer stand. 21 October (the 1969 revolution) has not been kept since 1991, and Villa Somalia's footer (read 30 October) names 15 May and 12 October, which the 1972 law lacks. The 2026 declarations are still not found. Do not model from the 1972 list without the new Code.

sources.title: Lao Official Gazette: ດຳລັດ ວ່າດ້ວຍ ວັນພັກ (Decree on Holidays), Government, No. 386/ລບ, Vientiane, 15.12.2017 (listed under the Ministry of Home Affairs, published 31-05-2018, status 'ປັດຈຸບັນ' current); scanned, 2 pages
sources.said: Cites the Labour Law No. 43/NA of 24 December 2013. Art. 3: 'ວັນພັກປະຈຳອາທິດ ໝາຍເຖິງ ວັນເສົາ ແລະ ວັນອາທິດ' (weekly rest: Saturday and Sunday); 'ວັນພັກຊົດເຊີຍ ໝາຍເຖິງ ວັນພັກທົດແທນ ວັນພັກທາງລັດຖະການ ທີ່ກົງກັບ ວັນເສົາ ຫຼື ວັນອາທິດ' (a compensatory day replaces an official holiday falling on a Saturday or Sunday). Art. 4, official holidays: 'ວັນທີ 01 ມັງກອນ (ວັນປີໃໝ່ສາກົນ); ວັນທີ 08 ມີນາ (ວັນແມ່ຍິງສາກົນ); ວັນບຸນປີໃໝ່ລາວ (ວັນສັງຂານລ່ອງ, ວັນສັງຂານເນົາ ແລະ ວັນສັງຂານຂຶ້ນ); ວັນທີ 01 ພຶດສະພາ (ວັນກຳມະກອນສາກົນ); ວັນທີ 02 ທັນວາ (ວັນຊາດ ສປປ ລາວ)'. Art. 5: the Prime Minister's Office issues notice of the compensatory days. Signed Thongloun Sisoulith, Prime Minister.

entries.foundInPart: Found: the Decree on Holidays No. 386/Gov of 15 December 2017 (Lao Official Gazette), art. 4: 1 January, 8 March, Lao New Year (three days, not dated by the decree), 1 May, 2 December; a holiday on a Saturday or Sunday has a compensatory day the Prime Minister’s Office announces (art. 3, 5). Missing: the 2026 notice with the New Year’s days and the compensatory days, so no year is whole.

sources.title: Acceso a la Justicia, glossary: Días festivos, quoting article 184 of the Ley Orgánica del Trabajo, los Trabajadores y las Trabajadoras (G.O.E. N° 6.076 of 7 May 2012)
sources.said: Artículo 184 ... Son días feriados, a los efectos de esta Ley: a) Los domingos; b) El 1º de enero; lunes y martes de carnaval; el Jueves y el Viernes Santos; el 1º de mayo y el 24, 25 y el 31 de diciembre; c) Los señalados en la Ley de Fiestas Nacionales; y d) Los que se hayan declarado o se declaren festivos por el Gobierno Nacional, por los Estados o por las Municipalidades, hasta un límite total de tres por año.

sources.title: El Diario, Estos son los días feriados y bancarios de 2026 en Venezuela (2 December 2025)

Domingo 19 de abril; Domingo 5 de julio. (The bank-only Mondays it lists besides are the banking law's, not the LOTTT's.)

sources.title: Gaceta Oficial de la República Bolivariana de Venezuela N° 6.998 Extraordinario (17 March 2026): Decreto N° 5.276
sources.said: Decreto Nº 5.276, mediante el cual se declara día de júbilo nacional, No laborable, el día 18 de marzo de 2026, a los fines de que los venezolanos y las venezolanas, a lo largo de todo el territorio nacional, puedan incorporarse a las actividades de celebración de la conquista histórica del campeonato del Clásico Mundial de Béisbol. (The Gaceta's summaries searched for 2025-2026: 'feriado', 'no laborable', 'no laborables', 'júbilo', 'duelo nacional', 'asueto', 'se declara día': no other non-working day; the seven days of national mourning of January 2026, Decreto N° 5.206, are not days off.)

entries.sought: Zambia's public holidays, the days off its law or its government's list names, nationally and in each first-level region that keeps its own

sources.title: Public Holidays Act, 1964 (Chapter 272), as at 31 December 1996 (Laws.Africa for ZambiaLII, from the Ministry of Legal Affairs' revised edition)
sources.said: 2. (1) The days mentioned in the Schedule shall be observed throughout Zambia as public holidays. (2) Whenever any of the days mentioned in the Schedule falls on a Sunday, the following Monday shall be observed as a public holiday. 3. The Minister shall have power, by statutory notice, from time to time to declare that any day or days shall be observed in Zambia as public holidays in addition to the days mentioned in the Schedule ... Schedule: (a) New Year's Day (b) Youth Day (12th March) (c) Good Friday (d) Holy Saturday (e) Lbour Day (1st May) (f) African Freedom Day (25th May) (g) Heroes Day (First Monday in July) (h) Unity Day (Tuesday following Heroes Day) (i) Farmers Day (First Monday in August) (j) Independence Day (24th October) (k) Christmas Day [As amended by Act No. 23 of 1987]

sources.title: Statutory Instrument No. 33 of 2007, The Public Holiday (Declaration) Notice, 2007 (Government Gazette of 27 April 2007)
sources.said: 2. It is hereby declared that the 8th of March in every year, commencing with 8th March, 2008, shall be observed as a public holiday in commemoration of the International Women's day.

sources.title: National Assembly of Zambia, Report of the Committee on Governance, Housing and Chiefs' Affairs on the Public Holidays (Amendment) Bill, N.A.B. No. 76 of 2026
sources.said: Zambia currently observes sixteen public holidays annually ... under section 3 of the principal Act, the Minister retains powers to declare additional public holidays by statutory notice. These include International Women's Day, Kenneth Kaunda Day, Easter Monday and the National Day of Prayer, Fasting, Repentance and Reconciliation. ... the "Sunday rule" practically applies to eight (8) holidays.

sources.title: News Diggers, Govt, churches move National Day of Prayer to Dec 29 (9 October 2026)

sources.title: News Diggers, Moving National Day of Prayer to Dec 29 is "satanic betrayal" - Sumaili (10 October 2026)
sources.said: In 2015, late former president Edgar Lungu declared October 18 as an annual public holiday to observe the National Day of Prayer, Fasting, Repentance and Reconciliation.

sources.title: News Diggers, Only Thursday is a public holiday, govt tells workers (11 August 2026)
sources.said: Kangwa says government has declared Thursday, August 13, as a public holiday to allow workers to cast their votes.

sources.title: News Diggers, Cabinet declares inauguration day a holiday (31 August 2026)

entries.sought: Uganda's public holidays, the days off its law or its government's list names, nationally and in each first-level region that keeps its own

sources.title: Public Holidays Act (Chapter 174), as at 31 December 2023 (revised and consolidated by the Law Reform Commission of Uganda; Laws.Africa for ULII)
sources.said: 2. (1) The days specified in Schedule 2 to this Act are declared to be public holidays, which, subject to this Act, shall in every year be kept and observed as public holidays throughout Uganda. (2) In addition ... the President may declare any other day to be a public holiday, and may limit the observation of any such public holiday to any area or place in Uganda. ... Schedule 2: Archbishop Janan Luwum Day - 16th February; Birth of Prophet Muhammed Day; Boxing Day - 26th December; Christmas Day - 25th December; Easter Monday; Good Friday; Idd Adhua; Idd el-Fitr Day; Idd-ul-Zuho Day; Independence Day - 9th October; Labour Day - 1st May; Martyrs’ Day - 3rd June; National Heroes Day - 9th June; New Year’s Day - 1st January; Women’s Day - 8th March. (Idd Adhua and Idd-ul-Zuho are both names of the feast of sacrifice, kept once.)

sources.title: Office of the President, State House of The Gambia, 'The Office of the President Announces Christmas and New Year Public Holidays' (23 December 2025)
sources.said: 'His Excellency President Adama Barrow has declared Thursday 25th December and Friday 26th December 2025 ... Christmas and Boxing Day, as public holidays throughout The Gambia. Additionally, Thursday 1st January 2026 has also been declared as a public holiday as part of the New Year celebrations.'

sources.title: Office of the President, 'Declaration of Eid-Ul-Fitr Public Holidays' (18 March 2026)
sources.said: '... is pleased to declare Thursday, 19th March and Friday, 20th March 2026 as public holidays nationwide in observance of Eid ul-Fitr, locally known as "Koriteh."'

sources.title: Office of the President, 'Declaration of Public Holidays' (31 March 2026)
sources.said: '... is pleased to declare Friday, 3rd April and Monday, 6th April 2026 as public holidays throughout the country in observance of the Christian feast of Good Friday and Easter Monday.'

sources.title: Office of the President, 'Declaration of Public Holiday' (29 April 2026)
sources.said: '... is pleased to declare Friday, 1st May 2026, as a nationwide public holiday in observance of International Workers' Day.'

sources.title: Office of the President, 'Declaration of Public Holiday' (23 June 2026)
sources.said: '... has declared Thursday, 25th June 2026, as a public holiday throughout the country in observance of Yawm al-Ashura.'

sources.title: Office of the President, 'Declaration of Public Holiday' (13 August 2026)
sources.said: '... has declared Saturday, 15th August 2026, as a public holiday throughout the country in observation of the Christian feast of Assumption Day, Commonly known as "Sang Marie".'

sources.title: Office of the President, 'Declaration of Public Holiday' (21 August 2026)
sources.said: '... has declared Wednesday, 26th August 2026 as a public holiday throughout the country in observance of "Maulid Al-Nabi," ... on the 12th of Rabat- Al Awwal 1448 Hijra which coincides with the 25th August 2026.'

entries.foundInPart: Found: the Office of the President’s 2026 declarations of 1 January, 19-20 March (Koriteh), 3 and 6 April, 1 May, 25 June (Ashura), 15 August (Assumption) and 26 August (Maulid). Missing: the Public Holidays Act’s Schedule; 18 February (Independence Day) and Christmas and Boxing Day 2026, not declared yet; Africa Day (25 May) and Tobaski (27-28 May), which only Gambiana reports.
