entries.sought: The tax on a screen worker's pay in Belize

sources.title: Taxes in Belize (BELTRAIDE, Belize Trade and Investment Development Service)
sources.said: Income tax is levied at a rate of 25% on the taxable income of employed residents in Belize whose annual earnings exceed BZ$26,000 (US$13,000). Individuals earning less than this amount are exempt from income tax. The basic allowance is BZ$25,600 (US$12,800). … Income Tax 25% on incomes above BZ$29,000 per year. … This tax, known as PAYE, applies exclusively to employee income and is not considered a cost to be borne by the employer or business. … Businesses, companies, and self-employed persons with annual earnings exceeding BZ$75,000 are required to pay business tax. … Professional Services 6.0% Commissions & Royalties 5.0% - 15.0% … Belize's General Sales Tax (GST) is a 12.5% consumer tax on goods and services. … Businesses with annual turnover exceeding $75,000 (US$37,500) from taxable activities must register for GST with the Department of GST.

sources.title: Contribution & Benefit Schedule, effective 4 April 2022 (Social Security Board, Belize)
Income and Business Tax Act, Chapter 55, Revised Edition 2020 (laws as at 31 December 2020), Attorney General's Ministry of Belize
sources.said: does not exceed twenty six thousand dollars … $25,600.00 … in the case of all other employed individuals … $19,600.00 … income of every employed person shall be charged at the rate of … twenty-five per centum of the chargeable income … “basis year” means the calendar year coinciding with the year of … last day of the third month following the end of the basis year a … return of income for that year in the form prescribed and … employee need not file a return if his only income was … A person not resident in Belize, in this section referred … to as a non-resident person, shall be assessable and chargeable … Every person who pays any management fees, rental of … plant or equipment, or charges for technical services and … insurance premium to a non-resident shall deduct therefrom tax … at the rate of twenty-five percent of such payment … “management fees” means payment for the provision of … industrial or commercial advice or for management or technical … services or similar services or facilities … withholding tax at the rate of three per centum of such payments … Where the gross contract payment is less than three … thousand dollars the provisions of this section shall not apply

sources.title: Income Tax Threshold Raised, Wider Relief for Middle-Class Workers (The Reporter, 22 September 2024)
sources.said: Effective Janu … ary 1, 2025, Be … lizean workers earning less than $29,000 annually will be exempt from paying in … come tax

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: Cabo Verde, Individual - Taxes on personal income (reviewed 29 May 2026)
sources.said: Taxable income (CVE*) Tax rate (%) Over Not over 0 960,000 16.5 960,000 1,800,000 23.1 1,800,000 27.5 … An exemption from taxation applies to net income of up to CVE 220,000 annually. … Non-resident individuals are subject to PIT only on Cabo Verdean-source income at flat tax rates that are the same as those applicable for resident taxpayers.

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: Cabo Verde, Individual - Tax administration (reviewed 29 May 2026)
sources.said: As a rule, the tax year coincides with the calendar year (i.e. 1 January to 31 December). … taxpayers must compute the tax due and file a tax return by 31 May of the following year. … Any outstanding tax liability must be paid by 31 August of the year in which the return is due.

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: Cabo Verde, Individual - Other taxes (reviewed 29 May 2026)
sources.said: the contributions are due on the employee’s gross remuneration at rates of 8.5% and 16% by the employee and the employer, respectively. … The contributions applicable to self-employees corresponds to a fixed rate of 19.5%. … The VAT system in Cabo Verde closely follows the European Union (EU) VAT system and is assessed at the standard rate of 15%.

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: Cabo Verde, Individual - Income determination (reviewed 29 May 2026)
sources.said: 1 0 80,000 15 5,500 2 80,000 150,000 21 10,300 3 150,000 25 16,300 … Business and professional income earned by individual entrepreneurs under standard organised accounting are subject to WHT at the rate of 20% as an advance payment on account of the final annual income tax liability.

sources.title: Boletim Oficial I Série n.º 7, 23 January 2015: Decreto-Lei n.º 6/2015 (withholding regime)
sources.said: Estão sujeitos a retenção na fonte à taxa de 20% (vinte por cento), por conta do imposto devido a final, os rendimentos empresariais e profissionais relativos à prestação de serviços … Artigo 8.º Rendimentos da categoria B 1. Estão sujeitos a retenção na fonte à taxa de 20% (vinte por cento), por conta do imposto devido a final, os rendimentos empresariais e profissionais relativos à prestação de serviços, obtidos em território nacional, pagos ou colocados à disposição por entidades que disponham ou devam dispor de contabilidade organizada … 3. A taxa é aplicada ao rendimento ilíquido sujeito a retenção, antes da liquidação do Imposto Sobre Valor Acrescentado (IVA) a que haja lugar. … Artigo 13.º Rendimentos de não residentes 1. Os rendimentos obtidos em território nacional por não residentes, que não sejam imputáveis a estabelecimento estável nele situado, estão sujeitos a retenção na fonte, através da aplicação das taxas referidas nos artigos anteriores, que revestirão sempre caráter liberatório, sem opção de englobamento.

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: Cabo Verde, Corporate - Withholding taxes (reviewed 29 May 2026)
sources.said: Royalty payments are subject to WHT at the rate of 20%.

sources.title: Czech Republic Highlights 2026 (Deloitte International Tax)
sources.said: The 23% tax rate is applicable to income exceeding 36 times the average wage for the calendar year (CZK 1,762,812 for 2026). … Tax year: The tax year is the calendar year. … Where a tax return is required, it generally must be filed and any tax liability must be paid by 1 April of the following year. The deadline is 1 May of the following year if a tax return that is not filed by 1 April is subsequently filed electronically by the taxpayer, or 1 July of the following year if a tax return that is not filed by 1 April is subsequently filed by a tax advisor. … Tax on employment income is withheld by the employer and remitted to the tax authorities. Self- employed individuals (entrepreneurs) generally must file a tax return but have the option to be subject to a lump-sum tax … An employer contributes 9% of the employee’s gross salary to the state health insurance funds and 24.8% of the employee’s gross salary to the state social security funds. An employee contributes 11.6% of gross income (4.5% health insurance, 6.5% old-age pension, 0.6% sickness insurance). A self-employed individual is subject to a mandatory contribution of 42.7% (13.5% health insurance, 28% old-age pension, 1.2% unemployment) on the assessment base (determined as at least 55% of the income tax base). … There is no maximum assessment base for health insurance purposes. The maximum assessment base for social security purposes (i.e., old-age pension contributions and unemployment insurance, applicable in the case of both the employee and the employer, as well as for a self-employed individual) is 48 times the average wage for the calendar year (CZK 2,350,416 for 2026). … A 35% rate applies where dividends are paid to a resident of a non- EU or non-EEA jurisdiction with which the Czech Republic does not have a tax treaty or a tax information exchange agreement (TIEA). … The standard VAT rate is 21%. A reduced rate of 12% applies to certain supplies … A Czech company must register for VAT if its supplies in the Czech Republic exceed CZK 2 million in a calendar year. In this case, the Czech company will become a VAT payer starting from 1 January of the following year. However, if a Czech company’s supplies in the Czech Republic exceed CZK 2,536,500 in a calendar year, the company will become a VAT payer on the date immediately following the date this threshold is exceeded.

sources.title: Personal Income Tax (Inland Revenue Division, Dominica)
sources.said: All individuals who are considered resident are required to furnish returns to the Inland Revenue Division by March 31st each calendar year. sources.title: Pay As You Earn (P.A.Y.E.) (Inland Revenue Division, Dominica)

sources.title: Withholding Tax (Inland Revenue Division, Dominica)

sources.title: Value Added Tax (VAT) (Inland Revenue Division, Dominica)
sources.said: The tax is imposed at a rate of 15% of the value of every taxable supply by a taxable person in Dominica except if the supply is classified as accommodations & diving activity which carries a rate of 10%

sources.title: Loi n° 21-16 du 30 décembre 2021 portant loi de finances pour 2022, Journal officiel de la République algérienne n° 100 (copy held by SIPRI)
sources.said: Le revenu net annuel tel que déterminé par les dispositions de l’article 85 du présent code est soumis à l’impôt sur le revenu global au lieu du domicile fiscal, suivant le barème progressif ci-après : FRACTION DU REVENU IMPOSABLE EN DINARS TAUX D’IMPOSITION N’excédant pas 240.000 DA de 240.001 DA à 480.000 DA de 480.001 DA à 960.000 DA de 960.001 DA à 1.920.000 DA de 1.920.001 DA à 3.840.000 DA Supérieure à 3.840.000 DA 0% 23% 27% 30% 33% 35% … III. POUR LES REVENUS REALISES PAR LES PERSONNES PHYSIQUES N’AYANT PAS LEUR DOMICILE FISCAL EN ALGERIE : … 24%, pour les revenus énumérés à l’article 33 du présent code, versés par des débiteurs établis en Algérie ; … 15%, pour les sommes versées sous forme de cachets ou droits d’auteur, aux artistes ayant leur domicile fiscal hors d’Algérie. Toutefois, ne sont pas comprises dans la base de l’impôt sur le revenu global (IRG), les sommes perçues par ces mêmes artistes lorsqu’ils interviennent dans le cadre d’accords d’échanges culturels, des fêtes nationales, festivals et manifestations culturelles et artistiques, organisés sous la tutelle du ministère de la culture et de l’office national de la culture et de l’information … « Art. 31 bis. — Les contribuables réalisant des revenus relevant de la catégorie des bénéfices des professions non commerciales prévus à l’article 22 ci-dessus, sont soumis au régime simplifié des professions non commerciales. Ces contribuables doivent mentionner sur une déclaration spéciale, le montant des recettes encaissées, celui des dépenses décaissées et le résultat réalisé au titre de l’année considérée. Ils sont tenus de souscrire et de faire parvenir cette déclaration au service des impôts du lieu d’activité, au plus tard, le 30 avril de chaque année. … Sont exclus de ce régime d’imposition : … 9-les professions non commerciales.

entries.sought: The tax on a screen worker's pay in Ecuador

sources.title: Ecuador: individual/taxes-on-personal-income (PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, reviewed 23 July 2026)
sources.said: 0 12,208 - 0 12,208 15,549 - 5 15,549 20,188 167 10 20,188 26,700 631 12 26,700 35,136 1,412 15 35,136 46,575 2,678 20 46,575 62,005 4,965 25 62,005 82,679 8,823 30 82,679 109,956 15,025 35 109,956 Onwards 24,572 37 … There are no local (provincial, county, or municipal) taxes on income. … Non-residents are subject to 25% income tax on income received from local sources, which is withheld at source. Payments made to non-residents occasionally working in Ecuador, when not charged to an Ecuadorian company or branch of a foreign entity, do not give rise to income tax.

sources.title: Ecuador: individual/other-taxes (PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, reviewed 23 July 2026)
sources.said: Private employees under a labour relationship will contribute at the rate of 9.45% of remuneration arising from employment … Voluntary contributors must pay a rate of 17.6% over their income. The employer contribution amounts to 12.15% of total remuneration. … Personal services provided under a professional fee contract relationship are subject to VAT at 15%, which, when provided to companies, is subject to 100% withholding by them. Professionals are required to file VAT returns.

sources.title: Ecuador: individual/tax-administration (PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, reviewed 23 July 2026)
sources.said: In the case of employees, there is mandatory monthly withholding by the employer as long as the total annual net income exceeds the non-taxable base of USD 12,208. … The employer's annual withholding return is considered the employee's income tax return. … The fiscal year is the calendar year. … Other individuals must file their income tax return in March of the following year.

sources.title: El SRI expide nuevos porcentajes de retención en la fuente de Impuesto a la Renta (NMS Law, 2 March 2026), reproducing SRI Resolution NAC-DGERCGC26-00000009
sources.said: Mediante la Resolución NAC-DGERCGC26-00000009, de 27 de febrero de 2026, el Servicio de Rentas Internas expidió el régimen actualizado de porcentajes de retención en la fuente del Impuesto a la Renta, aplicable a partir del 1 de marzo de 2026 … 10 % a) Honorarios, comisiones y demás pagos realizados a personas naturales residentes en el país que presten servicios en los que prevalezca el intelecto sobre la mano de obra, indistintamente de que el prestador del servicio posea o no título profesional o la relación del título con la actividad realizada. b) Honorarios, comisiones, regalías y demás pagos realizados a personas naturales y sociedades, nacionales o extranjeras, residentes en el Ecuador, por el ejercicio de actividades relacionadas directa o indirectamente con la utilización o aprovechamiento de su imagen o renombre, incluidos artistas … Se añade una regla general del 3% para pagos no contemplados en porcentajes específicos

sources.title: Boletín informativo 08-2026: Resolución SRI NAC-DGERCGC26-00000009 (Procuraduría, Universidad Técnica Particular de Loja, 25 March 2026)
sources.said: Mediante Registro Oficial - Cuarto Suplemento Nro. 233, de fecha 27 de febrero de 2026, el Servicio de Rentas Internas, emite la resolución Nro. NAC-DGERCGC26-00000009, a través de la cual entró en vigencia un nuevo esquema de retenciones en la fuente del Impuesto a la Renta.

entries.sought: The tax on a screen worker's pay in Estonia

sources.title: Tax rates (Estonian Tax and Customs Board)
sources.said: 2026 The rate of withheld income tax is 22%. The basic exemption is 700 euros per month, i.e. 8,400 euros per year, or 776 euros per month, i.e. 9,312 euros per year at pensionable age . … The rate of social tax is 33 per cent. The monthly rate of the minimum social tax obligation is 886 euros , i.e. the minimum obligation of social tax is 292.38 euros per month. The unemployment insurance premium rates are 1.6% for the employee and 0.8% for the employer (the same as in 2025). … The funded pension contribution rate is 2%, 4% or 6%, depending on a person's application to the registrar. If a person has not made an application to use a higher rate, the default contribution rate is 2%. … VAT rates are 24% (standard rate) , 13%, 9%, and 0%.

sources.title: Calculation of basic exemption (Estonian Tax and Customs Board)
sources.said: From 2026, the basic exemption is 700 euros per month, i.e. up to 8,400 euros per year. The difference compared with previous years is that the basic exemption no longer depends on a person's income … If employees do not submit an application for using basic exemption, employers must withhold income tax from the first euro (basis: subsection 2 of § 42 of the Income Tax Act ).

sources.title: Estonia - Individual - Taxes on personal income (PwC, reviewed 29 May 2026)
sources.said: Local income taxes There are no local taxes on income.

sources.title: Estonia - Individual - Other taxes (PwC, reviewed 29 May 2026)
sources.said: Social tax paid by employers is not capped and mainly applies to salaries, directors’ fees, and service fees paid and fringe benefits granted to individuals. The period of taxation is a calendar month. The net business income derived by individuals registered as sole proprietorships is also subject to 33% social tax (capped). Sole proprietorships are required to make quarterly advance payments of social tax in fixed amounts

sources.title: Estonia - Corporate - Withholding taxes (PwC, reviewed 29 May 2026)
sources.said: Payments for the activities of non-resident artists or sportsmen carried out in Estonia are subject to a 10% WHT rate. … Royalties (including payments for the use of industrial, commercial, or scientific equipment) paid to non-residents are generally subject to a 10% WHT rate under domestic law … Royalties and rental payments to resident individuals are subject to a 22% WHT rate.

sources.title: Estonia - Individual - Tax administration (PwC)
sources.said: For non-residents, the tax withheld at source at domestic or treaty rates generally constitutes final tax as regards their Estonian-source income, and the non-resident is generally not obligated to submit a tax return … The period of taxation is a calendar year. Tax returns In general, resident individuals must file an individual tax return by 30 April following the year in which the income arises. … must pay the final amount of income tax due by 1 October of the year following the period of taxation.

sources.title: Estonia - Corporate - Other taxes (PwC)
sources.said: If the taxable supplies of Estonian resident businesses or a fixed establishment of a non-resident business in Estonia exceed EUR 40,000 in a calendar year, VAT registration is required.

entries.sought: The tax on a screen worker's pay in Egypt

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: egypt Individual - Taxes on personal income
sources.said: Earned income (EGP*) Tax rate on bracket (%) From 1 to 40,000 0 40,000 to 55,000 10.0 55,000 to 70,000 15.0 70,000 to 200,000 20.0 200,000 to 400,000 22.5 400,000 to 1,200,000 25.0 More than 1,200,000 27.5 … Please note that both residents and non-residents are entitled to an annual salary tax exemption of EGP 20,000. … The above-mentioned brackets also apply to non-residents on the income they receive from an Egyptian treasury or against work performed in Egypt.

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: egypt Individual - Tax administration
sources.said: The taxable period is the calendar year starting 1 January and closing on 31 December … The submission deadline for an individual is on or before 31 March following the end of the fiscal year to which the return relates. … Tax on employment income is withheld at source on a monthly basis. Employers are required to file quarterly tax statements in January, April, July, and October of each year.

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: egypt Individual - Other taxes
sources.said: The employee contribution percentage is 11% of the total social insurance salary. … as of 1 January 2026, the minimum social insurance salary is EGP 2,700, whereas the maximum is EGP 16,700. … The employer contribution percentage is 18.75% of the total social insurance salary.

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: egypt Corporate - Withholding taxes
sources.said: Service payments are subject to the 20% WHT. … Royalty payments are subject to 20% WHT.

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: egypt Corporate - Other taxes
sources.said: VAT registration is mandatory for any person whose annual taxable turnover exceeds EGP 500,000, in accordance with the provisions of the VAT law. … the standard VAT rate is 14% (previously 13%)

sources.title: قانون الضريبة على الدخل رقم 91 لسنة 2005 (Income Tax Law 91 of 2005, consolidated), manshurat.org
sources.said: المادة 56 تخضع للضريبة بسعر 20% المبالغ التي يدفعها أصحاب المنشآت الفردية والأشخاص الاعتبارية المقيمة في مصر والجهات غير المقيمة التي لها منشأة دائمة في مصر لغير المقيمين في مصر وذلك دون خصم أي تكاليف منها. وتشمل هذه المبالغ ما يأتي: … 4- مقابل نشاط الرياضي أو الفنان سواء دفع له مباشرةً أو من خلال أي جهة. … بحجز مقدار الضريبة المستحقة وتوريدها إلى المصلحة في أول يوم عمل تال لليوم الذي تم فيه حجز الضريبة. التعديل الأخير بموجب القانون رقم 101 لسنة 2012

sources.title: قانون رقم 148 لسنة 2019 بإصدار قانون التأمينات الإجتماعية والمعاشات وفقاً لآخر تعديل (Social Insurance and Pensions Law 148 of 2019, consolidated), Alber Onsy law office
sources.said: ثانيا- أصحاب الأعمال، ومن في حكمهم: 1- الأفراد الذين يزاولون لحساب … 15- الأدباء والفنانين. … (أ) الحصة التي يلتزم بها صاحب العمل بواقع (12%) من أجور المؤمن عليهم العاملين لديه شهريا. (ب) الحصة التي يلتزم بها المؤمن عليه بواقع (9%) من أجره شهريا. 2- بالنسبة للفئات المشار إليها بالبندين ثانيا وثالثا بواقع (21%) من دخل الاشتراك الشهري الذي يختاره المؤمن عليه من الجدول المرفق باللائحة التنفيذية لهذا القانون. … وتزاد نسبة الاشتراكات كل سبع سنوات اعتبارا من تاريخ العمل بهذا القانون بنسبة (1%) وتقسم مناصفة بين صاحب العمل والمؤمن عليه، على ألا تتجاوز إجمالي نسبة الاشتراكات 26%.

sources.title: Fiscalité: un régime particulièrement avantageux pour les entreprises (Finances News Hebdo, 5 septembre 2021)
sources.said: l’exonération fiscale, une décision héritée du règne de Feu Hassan II, continue de prévaloir dans les régions de Laâyoune-Sakia El Hamra et Dakhla- Oued Ed-Dahab. … En clair, les entreprises établies à Laâyoune-Sakia El Hamra et Dakhla-Oued Ed-Dahab sont épargnées du paiement, entre autres, de l’IS et l’IR. … l’objectif de cette tradition fiscale, qui existant depuis les années 70, est de dynamiser les investissements dans le Sud marocain.

entries.sought: The tax on a screen worker's pay in Ethiopia

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, Ethiopia, Individual - Taxes on personal income (last reviewed 15 July 2026)
sources.said: Summary of monthly employment income tax brackets Sala ry (ETB) Income tax payable (%) From To 0 2,000 Exempt threshold 2,001 4,000 15 4,001 7,000 20 7,001 10,000 25 10,001 14,000 30 Over 14,000 35 … The same rates of tax are applicable to both residents and non-residents. … Non-residents are taxed on their Ethiopian-sourced income.

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, Ethiopia, Individual - Tax administration (last reviewed 15 July 2026)
sources.said: The tax year in Ethiopia runs from 8 July to 7 July. … Individuals who receive employment income only are not required to file personal income tax returns. … employers must withhold PAYE taxes from each payment to an employee and remit the payment to the tax authorities based on the amount withheld during each calendar month.

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, Ethiopia, Corporate - Withholding taxes (last reviewed 15 July 2026)
sources.said: Generally, payments for supply of goods (worth ETB 20,000 or more) and provision of services (worth ETB 10,000 or more) to a resident person are subject to WHT at the rate of 3%. … Royalties 10 (5 for art and culture) 10 Management fees 3 15 Technical fees 3 15

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, Ethiopia, Individual - Other taxes (last reviewed 15 July 2026)
sources.said: Employers are required to contribute 11% of the employee’s basic salary to the scheme, while the employee’s contribution is at 7%. … Foreign citizens with no Ethiopian origin are not allowed to contribute to the fund. … Value-added tax (VAT) is levied at a standard rate of 15% on the supply of taxable goods and services in Ethiopia.

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, Ethiopia, Corporate - Other taxes (last reviewed 15 July 2026)
sources.said: A person who, in the course of business, has supplied or expects to supply taxable goods or services whose value is ETB 2 million or more in a period of 12 months should register for VAT.

sources.title: Brief analysis on: Income Tax Proclamation No. 1395-2025 (Amendment), Grant Thornton Ethiopia

sources.title: Tvøroyrar kommuna, býráðsfundur 10.11.2025 (budget 2026)
sources.said: Í uppskotinum til fíggjarætlan 2026 er roknað við, at kommunuskattaprosentið og barnafrádrátturin framhaldandi verða ávikavist 20,9% og 8.000 kr.

sources.title: Løgtingslógarkunngerð nr. 109 frá 19. september 2023 um landsskatt og kommunuskatt (Skattalógin), logir.fo
sources.said: 1) Alt, sum er lagt inn í peningi fyri persónligt arbeiði í tænastu fyri onnur, heruppií løn, frítíðarløn, samsýning, tantiéme, provisjón ella líknandi. … Áðrenn A-inntøka verður goldin skattgjaldara, skal A-skattur avroknast í upphæddini. … Eftirhildin fyribilsskattur, smb. 63. §, 5. stk., má ikki vera meira enn 50% av tí einstøku útgoldnu A-inntøkuni. … § 2. Avmarkaða skattskyldu hevur hvør persónur … c) fáa gjald fyri nýtslugjald (royalty) úr Føroyum. … heruppií spælifilmar, filmar og bond til útvarps- og sjónvarpssendingar … h) fær inntøkur stavandi frá arbeiði, sum er gjørt her í landinum … 8) Samsýning í peningi og í hesum sambandi frítt vistarhald til persón, sum er til taks at gera arbeiði her í landinum … Reglurnar um, hvussu skatturin til landskassan fyri persónar, skatturin fyri feløg, deyðsbúgv v.m. sum hava fulla ella avmarkaða skattskyldu her á landi, verður útroknaður, verða ásettar við serstakari løgtingslóg. Í hesi lóg skal somuleiðis ásetast, hvørjir frádráttir skulu veitast í tí útroknaða landsskattinum. Stk. 2. Um samlaði inntøkuskatturin til land, kommunu og kirkju fer upp um 50% av skattskyldugu inntøkuni, verður tann ov nógv álíknaði inntøkuskatturin lækkaður lutfalsliga til landið, kommununa og kirkjuna.

sources.title: General about VAT (TAKS, the Faroese tax authority), archived 7 June 2026
sources.said: The VAT rate is 25% and is payable when sales of goods and taxable services are taking place at all stages in the chain of distribution within the Faroe Islands. … If your annual sale of goods and/or services amounts to less than DKK 50.000, you are not required to pay VAT to the Treasury. Furthermore, you are not required to add VAT on the sale of goods and/or services.

sources.title: Moving to the Faroes for work (TAKS, the Faroese tax authority), archived 10 May 2026
sources.said: If you only work in the Faroe Islands for a period of 180 days or less in a 12 month period and you do not move your permanent address to the Faroes, you are subject to limited tax liability in the Faroes. This means that you must pay a standard tax rate of 42% on all income earned in Faroes, but you remain tax liable in your country of residence. If you work onboard a FAS ship or a bareboat ship, the tax rate is 35%. … All individuals under the age of 67, regardless of whether they are subject to full or limited tax liability in the Faroe Islands, are required to contribute 3% of their income to the AM-fund. … Every time you are paid wages, your employer is responsible for making a holiday allowance contribution to TAKS' holiday fund. The contribution corresponds to 12% of your wages.

sources.title: Taxation in the Faroe Islands (TAKS, the Faroese tax authority), archived 9 May 2026
sources.said: Service Amount 2026 Health insurance ( Heilsutrygd ) DKK 175 p/m + 0.70% Parental benefits ( Barsilsgjald ) 0.86% Broadcast receiver license ( Kringvarpsgjald ) aged 24-66: DKK 176 p/m, aged 67+: DKK 72 p/m* Unemployment insurance ( ALS ) 0,6% Labour market pension fund ( Arbeiðsmarknaðareftirløn ) 3,0% Mandatory pension contribution ( kravd eftirløn ) 12% … B-income is income from self-employment … If you have full tax liability in the Faroe Islands, you start to pay taxes on income when you earn more than DKK 30,000 a year. … You start paying national tax on income over DKK 65,000 a year. The national tax is progressive … Each municipality sets its own tax rate which varies from 16% to 23%. … The church tax rate varies between 0.6% and 0.9% depending on your municipality.

sources.title: Deductions (TAKS), archived 10 May 2026
sources.said: if the child is under the age of 7, DKK 10,700 is deducted from the tax annually, and if the child is between 7 and 17, the tax deduction is DKK 7,500. In the local tax, it depends on the municipality and varies between DKK 5,100 and 12,000. … allows a married couple to move the basic deduction, up to DKK 30,000, among themselves

sources.title: Tax return (TAKS), archived 13 April 2026
sources.said: Ordinary taxpayers and self-employed are required to submit their tax return by 1 May. If you have not submitted your completed tax return by this date, TAKS is authorised to impose a fine of minimum DKK 1,000.

entries.sought: The tax on a screen worker's pay in Gabon

sources.title: Gabon – individual/taxes-on-personal-income (PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, last reviewed 6 August 2026)
sources.said: Q = [(S x 12) - A] / P (as Q is annual) P = Family quotient (number of shares). S = Monthly taxable gross income. A = 20% allowance. … 0 1,500,000 0 1,500,001 1,920,000 5% x Q - 75,000 1,920,001 2,700,000 10% x Q - 171,000 2,700,001 3,600,000 15% x Q - 306,000 3,600,001 5,160,000 20% x Q - 486,000 5,160,001 7,500,000 25% x Q - 744,000 7,500,001 11,000,000 30% x Q - 1,119,000 11,000,001 and above 35% x Q - 1,669,000 … The TCTS rate is 5% of the salary, indemnities, and emoluments paid to the taxpayer. The part of the revenue up to XAF 150,000 per month is exempted from the TCTS.

sources.title: Gabon – individual/tax-administration (PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, last reviewed 6 August 2026)
sources.said: The tax year is the calendar year in Gabon. … The counterfoil of the individual forms is given to the employees for their personal tax return, which must be filed before 1 March of each year. … The IRPP and the TCTS are withheld monthly by the employer and paid over (before the 15th day of the following month) to the Public Treasury.

sources.title: Gabon – individual/other-taxes (PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, last reviewed 6 August 2026)

Gross Income Based System Under the Gross Income Based System, the applicable income bands and tax rates for the 2025/26 tax year are as follows for income up to GBP 25,000: Taxable income Rate of tax (%) First GBP 10,000 6 Next GBP 7,000 20 Balance 28 The income bands and tax rates for income above GBP 25,000 are: Taxable income Rate of tax (%) (gross assessable income GBP 100,000 or less) First GBP 17,000 16 Next GBP 8,000 19 Next GBP 15,000 25 Next GBP 65,000 28 Remainder of assessable income 25 … The 'accrued in and derived from' principle is softened for individuals who carry out activities in Gibraltar for a period of less than 30 days in aggregate during the year of assessment, so that such individuals will be reimbursed for taxes paid on the income from their activities in Gibraltar.

sources.title: Gibraltar - Corporate - Withholding taxes (PwC, reviewed 22 August 2026)

sources.title: Gibraltar - Individual - Tax administration (PwC, reviewed 22 August 2026)
sources.said: Where the source of income is not collected under the PAYE system, individuals are required to make two payments on account, on 31 January and 30 June, in each year of assessment … The taxable period for individuals runs from 1 July, or the commencement of the source of income (if later), to 30 June in the year of assessment. … The due date for filing is 30 November.

sources.title: Pay as You Earn (PAYE) calculator (Gambia Revenue Authority)
Domestic Taxes FAQs (Gambia Revenue Authority)
sources.said: Any employee who earns incomes above D3, 000 per month or above D36, 000 annually arising from employment in The Gambia is subjected to employment income tax. … The rate of the PIT is the higher of the applicable tax rates in the 1st schedule or 1% of turnover for audited accounts or (2% of turnover in any other case). However, if business turnover is under D500, 000 per annum, then the tax liability is 3% of turnover. … Withholding tax is a deduction from payments made to contractors and subcontractors for the carrying out of work, supply of labour or materials and/or provision of technical/consultancy services. … The tax paid is an advance payment on behalf of the contractor/subcontractor. … The withholding tax rate on contracts is based on the contract price; 10% for Gambian residents, and 15% for non-residents … Employment income tax is charged on employment earnings through the Pay As You Earn (PAYE) system. … The standard VAT rate is 15 percent. This rate is applied to all goods and services unless they are specifically exempted. … All businesses with taxable supplies of at least D2, 000, 000 in a tax year are required to compulsorily register and charge VAT. In addition, businesses with taxable supplies of D1, 000, 000 and above in a tax year may voluntarily register.

sources.title: Personal Income Tax Brochure (Gambia Revenue Authority; rates "as at 2018")
sources.said: The rates of income tax imposed on the chargeable income of an individual or body of persons is as at 2018. … 1 D0 – D24,000 0% 2 D24,001 – D34,000 5% 3 D34,001 – D44,000 10% 4 D44,001- D54,000 15% 5 D54,001 – D64,000 20% 6 Above D64,000 25% … However, if business turnover is under D500, 000 per annum, then the tax liability is 3% of turnover. This is a final tax, … The tax year is the Calendar Year. … The closing dates for the payments of quarterly instalments are the 15th of the month following the end of the quarter. The closing date for filing and payment of final tax liability is 3 months after the end of the tax year.

sources.title: National Provident Fund (Social Security and Housing Finance Corporation, The Gambia)
sources.said: The contribution rate is 15% of basis salary of the employee, Five (5) per cent (%) of which is deducted from the employee’s wages’ while the remaining ten (10) per cent (%) is paid by the employer on behalf of the employee. … Any employer or employee to whom the Social Security and Housing Finance Corporation Act does not apply, may voluntarily register with the fund. Members registered voluntarily should declare their level of contribution based on their earnings.

sources.title: Federated Pension Scheme (SSHFC, The Gambia)
sources.said: The monthly contributions are entirely the responsibility of the employer and payments are calculated at 15% of the employees’ gross salary (i.e. basic plus all other fixed allowances combined).

sources.title: Industrial Injuries Compensation Fund (SSHFC, The Gambia)
sources.said: Under the IICF, the Act requires employers to pay the entire contribution each month on behalf of their workers. At present the contribution rate is 1% of total earnings; that is to say basic salary plus all other fixed allowances subject to a maximum contribution ceiling of D15.

sources.title: Gambia Revenue Authority, 8 December 2023: Press Release for Payment of Tax on Entertainment Events
sources.said: For the artist or musician (local or foreign) the tax shall be withheld by the promoter and paid to the GRA on their behalf. The applicable withholding tax rates are as follows: Local artist or musician – a withholding tax on the gross amount due to the artist or musician at the rate of 10% as specified under section 89(3) of the Income & Value Added Tax Act, 2012. Foreign or international artist or musician – a withholding tax on the gross amount due to the artist or musician at the rate of 15% as specified under sections 11 and 92 of the Income & Value Added Tax Act, 2012.

sources.title: Gambia Revenue Authority brochure: Withholding Tax on Contract Payments
sources.said: The withholding tax is based on the contract price or value of supply or service. The following are the types of withholding tax; • 10% for payments to non-resident Contractors, Suppliers or Service Providers

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: Equatorial Guinea, Taxes on personal income, quoting the New Equatorial Guinea Tax Code in force from 1 January 2025 (Ministerio de Hacienda y Presupuestos, minhacienda-gob.com)
sources.said: Individuals are subject to personal income tax (PIT) at the following rates. Yearly taxable income (XAF*) Tax rate (%) Over Not over 0 1,400,000 0 1,400,000 5,000,000 10 5,000,000 10,000,000 15 10,000,000 15,000,000 20 15,000,000 and above 25

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: Equatorial Guinea, Other taxes, quoting the Instituto Nacional de Seguridad Social, INSESO (inseso.org)
sources.said: The employer part of contributions to the National Institute of Social Security (INSESO for its Spanish acronym) is 21.5%. The employee part is 4.5%. The employer part of contributions to the Work Protection Fund (WPF) is 1%. The employee part is 0.5%. … The standard VAT rate is 15%. A rate of 0% is applicable to a specific list of products and equipment provided in the Tax Code (e.g. certain medical products, some equipment for construction). A reduced rate of 5% is applicable to a limited list of basic consumables and books.

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: Equatorial Guinea, Tax administration, quoting the New Equatorial Guinea Tax Code in force from 1 January 2025 (Ministerio de Hacienda y Presupuestos, minhacienda-gob.com)
sources.said: PIT calculated in accordance with the progressive tax scale is withheld monthly by the employer and then refunded to the Public Treasury during the first 15 days of the month following the month of payment of the salaries. … The taxable period is from 1 January to 31 December.

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: Equatorial Guinea, Withholding taxes, quoting the New Equatorial Guinea Tax Code in force from 1 January 2025 (Ministerio de Hacienda y Presupuestos, minhacienda-gob.com)
sources.said: According to the New EG Tax Code, there is a 10% tax withheld on the gross incomes obtained in Equatorial Guinea by non-resident entities. Therefore, as of 1 January 2025, all services provided to entities located in Equatorial Guinea will be subject to 10% WHT in Equatorial Guinea since the income is from an Equatorial Guinea source. There is a 10% WHT on royalties for non-CEMAC residents.

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: Greece, Individual - Tax administration (reviewed 8 September 2026)
sources.said: No taxable years other than the calendar year are permitted. … The submission of the Greek income tax returns takes place from 15 March to 15 July for each tax year. … The WHT on salaries, wages, and pensions is calculated on the amount of monthly salary after being reduced by the employee’s share of social security contributions, multiplied by 14 … The employer must withhold 1/14 of this amount each month from the employee’s salary.

sources.said: As of 1 January 2025, the social security contributions amount to 13.37% at the level of the employee and 21.79% at the level of the employer, i.e. 35.16% in total. The monthly social security contribution cap for the primary social security fund (EFKA) is set at EUR 7,761.94 from 1 January 2026. … The VAT rate is 24%. The reduced rate on basic necessities is 13%. A super reduced rate of 6% is also available for certain items.

sources.title: Guide to the Income Tax Ordinance (Government of South Georgia & the South Sandwich Islands, 2016)
sources.said: The rate of income tax is 7%. The tax system does not give any personal allowances and does not have any additional tax bands for higher earners. The 7% rate applies to all those liable to pay tax. … A person who earns income from work carried out in the Territory will pay income tax if they are resident in the Territory for either a continuous period of 183 days or more, or several shorter periods which total 183 days in a tax year. … pay the income tax that will be due on the employee’s earnings within 14 days of the end of each quarter. The employer will then make the appropriate deduction of tax from the person's pay. … If tax is deducted, and because of a change in circumstances the employee does not reside in the Territory for 183 days or more, then any tax paid will be refunded. … the obligation to pay income tax still starts once a person has been present in the Territory for 183 days. … The tax year runs from 1st January to the 31st December each year. … Tax must be paid within 60 days from the date of the demand.

sources.title: Jamaica Highlights 2026 (Deloitte International Tax)
sources.said: Rates: The first JMD 1,799,376 (JMD 1,902,360 as from 1 April 2026) of an individual resident’s income is tax free. Income earned in excess of the tax free threshold up to a total income of JMD 6 million is taxed at a rate of 25%. Taxable income exceeding JMD 6 million is taxed at 30%. … There are no personal allowances. … Tax year: The tax year is the calendar year. … Individuals must file a tax return and pay any tax due on or before 15 March of the year following the year of assessment. Advance payments of income tax are payable in four equal installments, due on or before the 15th day of March, June, September, and December of the year of assessment. … This tax usually is withheld from employment income by employers; however, where the income of an individual is not an emolument or where an employer is nonresident, the liable individual taxpayer must make the advance payments. … Employers are required to pay National Insurance Scheme (NIS) contributions at a rate of 3% of the remuneration paid to each employee, up to JMD 5 million per year per employee. Employers also are required to withhold 3% of each employee’s emoluments up to JMD 5 million per year and remit this amount to the NIS. Self-employed persons are required to contribute at a rate of 6% of earnings. Employers are required to make National Housing Trust contributions at a rate of 3%, while employees contribute at a rate of 2% on all taxable emoluments received from employment. Self-employed persons also are required to contribute at a rate of 3% of earnings. … Where an employer’s gross annual payroll exceeds JMD 173,328, the employer is required to make Human Employment and Resource Training Trust contributions, payable at a rate of 3% of the total emoluments of its employees. … An education tax is charged at a rate of 3.5% for employers and 2.25% for employees on emoluments after the deduction of NIS and approved superannuation scheme contributions. Self-employed persons are required to contribute at a rate of 2.25% of earnings. … Royalties: Royalties paid to residents are not subject to withholding tax. … The withholding tax rate is 15% on royalties paid to a resident of a CARICOM jurisdiction; otherwise, royalties paid to nonresident companies and individuals are subject to withholding tax at rates of 33.33% and 25% on the gross amount, respectively. … The standard GCT rate is 15%. … Registration: Registration is required by any person carrying on a taxable activity that has an annual turnover exceeding JMD 15 million.

sources.said: L'impôt des résidents saint-martinois est calculé par application d'un barème progressif. sources.title: Notice 2041-E: Personnes fiscalement domiciliées hors de France (DGFiP)
sources.said: les personnes résidant à Saint-Martin ou à Saint-Barthélemy qui ont transféré leur domicile fiscal dans ces collectivités après le 15 juillet 2007 et qui ne remplissent pas la règle de domiciliation fiscale de cinq ans dans ces collectivités(2) … Pour Saint-Martin, contrairement à Saint-Barthélemy, la règle de domiciliation fiscale de cinq ans s’applique seulement aux personnes physiques qui avaient leur domicile fiscal en France, en métropole ou dans les DOM avant de le transférer à Saint-Martin.

sources.title: Déclarer des revenus de source Saint-Martinoise (non-résidents) - Collectivité de Saint-Martin

Si vos revenus de source saint-martinoise représentent au moins 75 % de vos revenus totaux, les règles de droit commun s'appliquent.

sources.title: Déclaration de revenus (IR) - Résidents et assimilé résidents de Saint-Martin
sources.said: La déclaration annuelle doit être déposée au plus tard le 31 mai de chaque année, au titre des revenus perçus l'année précédente. Des acomptes provisionnels sont à régler au plus tard les 15 février et 15 mai.t. … L'impôt est ensuite calculé, puis recouvré par voie de rôle.

sources.title: New Caledonia - Individual - Taxes on personal income (PwC, reviewed 9 September 2026)
sources.said: Individuals, whether New Caledonian or foreign nationals, who have their tax domicile in New Caledonia are generally subject to personal income tax (PIT) on worldwide income (unless provided otherwise by a tax treaty between France and New Caledonia). … However, the tax saved from income splitting is generally limited to 300,000 CFP ( Communauté Française du Pacifique ) francs (XPF). For residents, progressive income tax rates are then applied as follows: Taxable income (XPF) Rate (%) Over Not over 0 1,000,000 0 1,000,000 1,800,000 4 1,800,000 3,000,000 12 3,000,000 4,500,000 25 4,500,000 40 … Generally, income derived by non-resident individuals is subject to a flat tax rate ( prélèvement forfaitaire ) of 25%. This tax applies to very broad types of revenues, notably employment and business or professional related income, pensions, investment income (unless subject to tax on financial incomes [IRVM]), royalties, and income from immovable property. A taxpayer is allowed to claim for the application of the progressive tax rate (as for resident) if one is in position to demonstrate that the progressive PIT would have been less than 25%.

sources.said: There are four rates of TGC: Reduced rate: 3% Specific rate: 6% Normal rate: 11% for all the operations that are not subject to another rate. Higher rate: 22%

sources.title: Questions fréquentes TGC (Direction des Services Fiscaux de Nouvelle-Calédonie)

sources.title: New Caledonia - Individual - Tax administration (PwC, reviewed 9 September 2026)
sources.said: Generally, the New Caledonian tax year runs from 1 January to 31 December. … each year before 1 April. … This deadline is extended to 30 June for taxpayers who do not have their tax domicile in New Caledonia. The income declaration filed electronically must reach the administration by 30 June at the latest … These payments should be made by 31 March and 15 July of each fiscal year.

sources.title: Déclaration de la retenue à la source (Direction des Services Fiscaux de Nouvelle-Calédonie)
sources.said: La retenue à la source s'applique aux rémunérations versées à des salariés détachés en Nouvelle-Calédonie par des entreprises établies hors de la Nouvelle-Calédonie. La base imposable de cette retenue est constituée par le montant net des sommes versées, après application de la déduction forfaitaire prévue au B de l'article Lp 97 et de l'abattement de 20 % résultant du II de l'article Lp 97, sous les mêmes conditions de plafond et limites. La retenue est calculée selon le tarif mentionné à l'article R 59-2 . Elle est libératoire de l'impôt sur le revenu.

sources.said: Toutes les personnes physiques domiciliées(1) en Polynésie française sont assujetties à la Contribution de Solidarité Territoriale sur les traitements, salaires, pensions, rentes viagères et indemnités diverses (CST-S) … 0,5 % à la fraction de revenus qui n’excède pas 150 000 F CFP 3% à la fraction de revenus compris entre 150 001 et 250 000 F CFP 5% à la fraction de revenus compris entre 250 001 et 400 000 F CFP 9% à la fraction de revenus compris entre 400 001 et 700 000 F CFP 11 % à la fraction de revenus compris entre 700 001 et 1 000 000 de F CFP 15 % à la fraction de revenus compris entre 1 000 001 et 1 250 000 de F CFP 18 % à la fraction de revenus compris entre 1 250 001 et 1 500 000 de F CFP 21 % à la fraction de revenus compris entre 1 500 001 et 1 750 000 de F CFP 24 % à la fraction de revenus compris entre 1 750 001 et 2 000 000 de F CFP 26 % à la fraction de revenus compris entre 2 000 001 et 2 500 000 de F CFP 28 % à la fraction de revenus supérieurs à 2 500 000 de F CFP … Lorsque le montant de la contribution est inférieur à 750 F CFP, soit pour tout revenu inférieur à 150 000 F CFP, elle n’est pas précomptée sur le salaire ou le revenu de remplacement. … Les employeurs et organismes de retraite ou de protection sociale doivent déclarer et reverser mensuellement la CST-S auprès de la recette des impôts de la DICP. sources.title: Wet Inkomstenbelasting 1922, consolidated to S.B. 2024 no. 3 (Belastingdienst Suriname)
sources.said: over het eerste gehele bedrag van SRD 108.000.- van het zuiver inkomen bedraagt de belasting nihil; … − van het gedeelte van het zuiver inkomen boven SRD 108.000, - tot en met SRD 150.000,- 8% − van het gedeelte van het zuiver inkomen boven SRD 150.000,- tot en met SRD 192.000,- 18% − van het gedeelte van het zuiver inkomen boven SRD 192.000.- tot en met SRD 234.000,- 28% − van het gedeelte van het zuiver inkomen boven SRD 234.000,- 38% … Ten aanzien van niet in Suriname wonende natuurlijke personen wordt de belasting geheven naar het binnenlands zuiver inkomen. … bedrijf, voor zover de daaruit verkregen winst kan worden toegerekend aan een in Suriname aanwezige vaste inrichting, met behulp waarvan het bedrijf wordt uitgeoefend; … dienstbetrekking, indien en voor zover daaruit opbrengst wordt verkregen ter zake van het vervullen of vervuld zijn van de dienstbetrekking in Suriname; … Het belastingjaar begint met 1 januari en eindigt met 31 december. … Uiterlijk de 15e april van het lopende belastingjaar dan wel uiterlijk binnen twee en een halve maand na aanvang van het lopend boek-jaar zijn, ook wanneer aan belastingplichtige geen voorlopig aangifte-biljet is uitgereikt, tot het doen van voorlopige aangifte verplicht … Binnen vier maanden na het einde van het belastingjaar of boekjaar dan wel van de belastingplicht, zo dit eerder is, zijn ook wanneer aan belastingplichtige geen aangiftebiljet is uitgereikt, tot het doen van definitieve aangifte verplicht

sources.title: Loonbelasting (Belastingdienst Suriname)
sources.said: De werkgever is inhoudingsplichtige: hij/zij moet de loonbelasting berekenen, inhouden en afdragen aan de Belastingdienst door middel van een aangifte loonbelasting en Premie A.O.V. … De LB-aangifte dient maandelijks vanaf de 26ste tot en met de 10de dag van de daaropvolgende maand te worden ingediend.

sources.title: Inkomstenbelasting (Belastingdienst Suriname)
sources.said: Met uitzondering van de buitenlandse belastingplichtige natuurlijke personen, geldt er voor alle natuurlijke personen een belastingvrije som. … De inkomstenbelasting is een aangifte belasting. Dat wil zeggen dat de belastingplichtige zelf moet aangeven wat zijn inkomen is geweest.

sources.title: BTW (Belastingdienst Suriname)
sources.said: Het algemene BTW-tarief bedraagt 10%. Dat betekent dat de levering en of invoer van goederen, alsook het verrichten van diensten belast is met 10% BTW. … U bent BTW-plichtig indien u gedurende een kalenderjaar een omzet behaalt van meer dan SRD 1.000.000, – door het verrichten van een of meerdere voor de BTW belaste activiteit(en).

sources.title: Wet Algemeen Oudedagsvoorzieningsfonds (S.B. 1981 no. 30, as last amended by S.B. 2002 no. 96), Belastingdienst Suriname
sources.said: Premieplichtig is de ingezetene van Suriname, al dan niet met de Surinaamse nationaliteit, die ingevolge de bepalingen van de “Inkom-stenbelasting 1922” winst uit bedrijf of beroep of loon uit dienstbe-trekking geniet en de leeftijd van 60 jaar nog niet heeft bereikt. … De grondslag van de heffing is het zuiver inkomen in de zin van de “Inkomstenbelasting 1922” en - ingeval loonbelasting verschuldigd is- het zuiver loon in de zin van de Wet Loonbelasting. … De hoogte van de premie bedraagt 4% (vier percent) van de heffings-grondslag. … De heffing van premie geschiedt bij wege van afdracht op aangifte, van aanslag en door inhouding op het loon.

sources.title: South Sudan Highlights 2026 (Deloitte International Tax)
sources.said: Taxable income (SSP) Rate* Up to 20,000 0% 20,001–40,000 5% 40,001–57,000 10% 57,001–90,000 15% Over 90,000 20% … Once the taxable income has been determined to fall under an income bracket, the whole of the taxable income is subjected to the tax rate applicable to that particular bracket (e.g., where taxable income is SSP 30,000, the 5% tax rate is applied to the whole amount and not only the amount in excess of SSP 20,000). … Monthly income of less than SSP 5,000 (zero rate). … Generally, the individual income tax rates for residents and nonresidents are progressive from 0% to 20%. … Tax year: The tax year is the calendar year. … The individual income tax return must be submitted before 1 April of the year following the tax period. A resident individual engaged in any entrepreneurial activity or receiving rental income must make advance quarterly payments of income tax. An employer must withhold income tax from an employee’s wages, including bonuses and allowances, for the appropriate payroll period. … Technical/consultancy fees or renumeration for part-time work paid to residents and nonresidents are subject to withholding tax at 20%. … An amount of 5% is deducted from an employee’s gross income as a contribution to the National Social Insurance Fund. … Nonresidents are subject to tax only on South Sudan-source income. … Royalties: Royalties paid to residents and nonresidents are subject to withholding tax at 10%. … Sales tax Rates Standard rate 18%/20% Reduced rate – Taxable transactions: Sales tax applies to manufacturers, importers, and service providers in South Sudan. Sales tax is imposed on the production of goods in South Sudan; the importation of goods and specified services such as hotel, restaurant, and bar services; and telecommunication services. … The rate charged ranges from 1% to 20%.

sources.title: Country Guide: Turks and Caicos Islands (Misick & Stanbrook, August 2022)
sources.said: Other than social security/national insurance payments, referred to in Section 6.6, there are no direct personal taxes in Turks and Caicos Islands (TCI). … With effect from April 1, 2022, the total liability for national insurance contributions is equivalent to 10 percent (increasing to 11 percent effective April 1, 2023, and 12 percent effective April 1, 2024), apportioned between the employer and employee as follows: • employers are required to pay 5.5 percent (increasing to 6 percent effective April 1, 2023, and 6.5 percent effective April 1, 2024); • employees are required to pay 4.5 percent (increasing to 5 percent effective April 1, 2023, and 5.6 percent effective April 1, 2024). … For the purposes of the liability, there is a salary cap of 4,000 dollars per month. Earnings of an employee of less than 25 dollars per week, or 108 dollars per month, are ignored. … There is a total liability for national insurance contributions amounting to 6 percent (salary cap for purposes of liability, 7,800 dollars per month, but with a minimum monthly contribution of 50 dollars). Of that 6 percent, the employer and the employee pay 3 percent each. … The employee contribution to national insurance and national health insurance is withheld from salary and deposited directly into the relevant funds along with the employer’s contribution. … There are no residency rules for tax purposes as there are no direct personal taxes in TCI. … Value Added Tax (VAT) There is no VAT in TCI.

sources.title: TAAF, Guide pratique de l'hivernant (September 2019), "Principes généraux du système fiscal des TAAF" and "Dix questions ... sur la contribution directe territoriale" (on arrêté territorial n° 2001-29 of 6 August 2001)
sources.said: La contribution directe territoriale (CDT) est un impôt direct proportionnel prélevé sur les revenus tirés d’une activité professionnelle exercée dans les TAAF, et versé aux TAAF par l’employeur. Elle fait l’objet de l’arrêté territorial n° 2001-29 du 6 août 2001, complété par la décision territoriale n° 2001-94. … La contribution directe territoriale est calculée sur la base d’un taux unique de 9% appliqué au montant brut des revenus perçus. Celui-ci est ramené à 6,3 % lorsque le domicile fiscal du contribuable est à La Réunion. … Les revenus imposables sont constitués par le montant brut des revenus perçus lors d’un séjour dans les TAAF, à l’exclusion des prestations familiales, des allocations spécifiques destinées à couvrir des frais, et des indemnités d’éloignement. … Si votre taux effectif d’imposition en métropole ou à La Réunion est inférieur au taux appliqué par les TAAF, ces dernières remboursent le trop prélevé. … Le calcul, la déclaration et le versement de la CDT sont effectués par l’employeur qui en adresse son montant chaque trimestre aux TAAF.

sources.title: BOI-RSA-GEO-30-20210506, Agents de l’État envoyés dans le territoire des TAAF et personnes relevant d’organismes appelés à intervenir dans ce territoire (BOFiP-Impôts, DGFiP)
sources.said: les agents de l’État et les personnes relevant d’organismes appelés à intervenir dans les TAAF qui sont envoyés dans ce territoire sont soumis à un impôt local sur le revenu. … L'arrêté n° 2001-29 du 6 août 2001 instaurant une contribution directe territoriale sur les revenus perçus dans le territoire des Terres australes et antarctiques françaises pris par l’administrateur supérieur du territoire, institue une contribution directe territoriale prélevée à la source par les employeurs sur les revenus perçus au titre d’une activité professionnelle exercée dans le territoire des TAAF. … L’impôt retenu à la source au titre d’une année s’impute sur l’impôt sur le revenu français dû au titre des revenus de cette même année, acquitté l’année suivante. … Lorsque les intéressés sont considérés comme fiscalement domiciliés hors de France, les rémunérations perçues à l’occasion de leur activité dans le territoire des TAAF ne sont pas soumises à l’impôt sur le revenu en France. … Les revenus professionnels correspondant à une activité exercée sur le territoire des TAAF sont soumis à une contribution directe territoriale. Cette contribution est retenue à la source par les employeurs et directement payée auprès de l’administration territoriale.

sources.said: Residents The amount of wage income tax payable for wages of residents of Timor-Leste can be calculated from this table: Monthly taxable wage Income tax rate 0 – $500 0% More than $500 10% of the amount over $500

sources.title: Autoridade Tributária de Timor-Leste: Annual Income Tax Return Guidelines
sources.said: Income Tax Rates Resident natural person Where the taxpayer is a resident natural person: Annual taxable income Tax on this income $0 – $6,000 0% More than $6,000 10%

sources.title: Timor-Leste Highlights 2026 (Deloitte)
sources.said: Employers are required to pay a monthly contribution towards an employee’s social security at a rate of 6% of the “contributory incidence basis.” … The employee’s contribution is payable at 4% of the contributory incidence basis and is withheld by the employer. … The obligation to withhold WIT rests with the employer. An employee in receipt of wages that have been correctly subject to WIT has no further liability to income tax on the amount received. … A 10% withholding tax applies to royalties paid to both residents and nonresidents. … For nonresident individuals, a flat rate of 10% applies on all income. … All other payments of Timor-Leste source income to nonresidents with no permanent establishment in Timor-Leste are subject to a 10% withholding tax where the payment is not for services identified above. … There is no VAT or similar tax in Timor-Leste (but see the sales tax description under “Other,” below); however, Timor-Leste is planning to introduce VAT … Tax year: The tax year is the calendar year. Filing status: … An annual income tax return must be filed and any income tax due paid by 31 March following the end of the tax year.

sources.said: Los menores entre catorce y diez y ocho años podrán ser empleados en empresas no industriales en las siguientes condiciones: a) Que hayan completado la instrucción primaria obligatoria o que el trabajo no impida su asistencia a la escuela; b) Que posean certificado de capacidad física y mental para el trabajo, expedido por la autoridad sanitaria competente; c) Que se trate de tareas diurnas, livianas, no peligrosas ni insalubres; d) Que medie autorización del representante legal del menor, visada por la autoridad competente; e) Que no trabajen más de cuatro horas diarias, ni más de veinticuatro semanales. entries.sought: Saint-Martin's mean daily maximum and minimum temperature and days of at least 1 mm, which no published normal gives (Météo-France publishes no fiche for its stations), as averages computed from Météo-France's own daily records by the WMO's rules, as R-0073's are

value.read: Grand-Case's (97127004) mean daily maximum and minimum, 2004-2013 (8 to 10 years a month), and Marigot Gendarmerie's (97127002) days of at least 1 mm, 1991-2020 (25 to 28 years a month): a town reads its own country's 1991-2020 station first, so Marigot's days of at least 1 mm stand over Grand-Case's 2004-2013 ones. Marigot's precipitation averages too, but Saint-Martin's precipitation is R-0060's (Marigot, 1971-2000), which comes first.
value.rules: As R-0073's (WMO-No. 1203, 2017): a month's mean none where 11 or more days are missing or 5 or more in a row (4.4.1 a), a month's sum (precipitation, sunshine) none where any day is (4.4.1 c), a count of days of at least 1 mm a share of the days observed (4.3.1 d), its average the mean share times the month's days, February's 28.25 (4.3.2); each month's average the mean of its valid values where they are of at least 80% of the period's years (4.4.2); the period each parameter's longest within 1991-2020 of ten years or more, from a year with a month of it to another, whose every month is averaged so, the latest of the longest. Rounded to a tenth (half up). Computed by tools/wmo/compile.ts as the stations compile. A day counts where its quality code (QRR, QTN, QTX) is 0 (protected: validated for good by the climatologist) or 1 (validated), not 2 (doubtful, under checking) or 9 (filtered: through the first checks only).
value.notFound: No station of Saint-Martin measures sunshine (none in the monthly file's INST); it stays blocked (R-0091).
value.ruling: An average computed from the service's own records, which the lead's ruling of 2026-11-02 lets stand as a normal, labelled to the player as R-0073's are (the official averages measured near a place, from the years they cover: weather.model).

value.notRead: The tables' 'Rain Days' (about 20 to 25 a month on 75 to 190 mm) state no threshold, so they aren't days of at least 1 mm; no sunshine is given. Both stay blocked (R-0092).
value.ruling: An average computed from the service's own records, which the lead's ruling of 2026-11-02 lets stand as a normal, labelled to the player as R-0073's are (the official averages measured near a place, from the years they cover: weather.model).

sources.said: Chapter 3: an average is the mean of monthly values over any specified period. 4.3.1-4.3.2: a count is a share of the days observed, its normal the mean share times the month's days, February's 28.25. 4.4.1: a mean is not calculated where 11 or more days are missing or 5 or more consecutive; a sum only with complete data; a count by the mean's rule. 4.4.2: a normal or average only where there are valid monthly values in at least 80% of the years of the averaging period.
